### AUD-150 — AUD-113's read-then-check convention bounds the decision, not the memory: the cap is applied after Data(contentsOf:) has already allocated the file

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** engine
- **Location:** `sources/TinyTitan/Infrastructure/ModelIO/VerifiedInstallReceipt.swift:96, sources/TinyTitanServer/Core/ModelCatalog.swift:287, sources/TinyTitan/Runtime/Prefill/ANEPrefillAttention.swift:182 (before); all three through BoundedMetadataRead.read (after)`
- **Category:** unbounded memory on an input file (found while converting AUD-142's sites)
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-142 fix, measurement of the shape AUD-113 chose

**Evidence before.** Three sites that AUD-113 recorded as fixed, and AUD-142's `evidence-before` as filed recorded as 'already bounded': `Data(contentsOf: url)` followed by `guard UInt64(data.count) <= maxBytes`. AUD-113's fix-summary names the reason — read, then check the size of the bytes actually read, because stat-then-re-read is a TOCTOU window — and that argument is sound about *which file* gets checked and wrong about *when the memory is spent*. Measured on this host, a 2 GiB sparse file (0 B allocated on disk, so the read is pure allocation, not page-cache) through `Data(contentsOf:)`: 0.350 s, `phys_footprint` +2,049 MB on a 24 GB Mac. The receipt path is reachable with a hostile install, which is exactly AUD-113's attacker model: a 2 GiB `verified-install.json` swaps the resident model out before the 64 MiB cap refuses it. The same shape sat in the sidecar reader and the catalog probe.

**Fix.** All three now call `BoundedMetadataRead.read(fileAt:maxBytes:)`, which `fstat`s the descriptor it is about to read and refuses before allocating — so both properties AUD-113 wanted hold at once: the size checked belongs to the file actually read (no K17 window), and the cap fires before the bytes exist. Error contracts are unchanged at each boundary by rewrapping `ModelError.metadataOverBound` into what each caller already catches: `trustedReceiptInvalid(detail:)` with the original wording, `CPUBackendError.unsupported`, `PrefillError.chunkedUnsupported`. BoundedMetadataRead's doc comment records the 2,049 MB measurement and why read-then-check is not the cheaper-safe option, so the convention cannot be re-adopted by mistake. AUD-113's own row is not rewritten; this row corrects it forward.

**Evidence after.** `BoundedMetadataReadTests.boundIsAppliedBeforeTheAllocation` is the guard: a 256 MiB sparse `tokenizer.json` refused at `maxBytes: 64`, asserting both the refusal text and that `phys_footprint` grew by less than 32 MiB. Mutation check: reinstating read-then-check fails that one assertion and nothing else (exit 1, `grew < 32` at line 61), then passes again when reverted — so the test is the only thing in the suite that can see this class, and it sees it. Existing AUD-113 tests still pass unchanged, which is the point of the rewrap: `anOversizedSidecarIsRefusedByTheBoundNotByTheDecoder`, `aScannedConfigOverTheBoundIsRefusedAndSaysSo`, and the receipt suite assert the same types and the same size-and-cap wording, now from a bound that precedes the allocation. Full serial suite and the qwen38-4 golden gate under AUD-142's evidence.

**Commit.** `65bf241`

### AUD-153 — The router test fixture's gate held one continuation for any number of waiters, so a second concurrent waiter hung the run

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier C
- **Project:** tooling
- **Location:** `tests/TinyTitanServer/RoutingFixtures.swift RoutingGate (wait/open); tests/TinyTitanServer/RoutingGateTests.swift`
- **Category:** test-infrastructure lost wake, found by AUD-143's own regression test
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-143 fix verification, 2026-10-06

**Evidence before.** Found while the AUD-143 stress test failed to drain. `RoutingGate.wait()` stored the continuation in a single `CheckedContinuation<Void, Never>?`, so a second waiter arriving before the gate opened overwrote the first and `open()` resumed only the last. That is reachable, not theoretical: the router allows several callers on the resident model at once (it is the HTTP coordinator that serialises requests), and one of seven release runs of the stress test measured `log.maxConcurrentGenerations == 2`, i.e. two generations inside the same gate. Two things came out of it. (1) `concurrentSwitchesWakeEveryQueuedCaller` reported `drained == false` for reasons that had nothing to do with the router. (2) Two diagnostic harnesses written to find out hung outright — 7 and 10 minutes with no output, killed by hand — because a task group joins every child and a child blocked on `await parkedTask.value` outlives both the timeout child and `group.cancelAll()`; cancelling the waiter does not cancel the unstructured task it awaits. Confirmed by `sample` of the hung helper: two threads, the main run loop idle in `mach_msg2_trap` and one parked `__workq_kernreturn`, nothing spinning — a lost wake, not a livelock, and no timer that could fire. Every measurement taken through this fixture before this row is suspect for the same reason the earlier AUD-143 release measurements were.

**Fix.** The gate now holds `[SuspensionSlot]`, one per waiter, and `open()` signals every one of them; a waiter that arrives after the open goes straight through, and a cancelled waiter is removed by identity and signalled `.cancel`, so it cannot be resumed twice. Same primitive as the production fix, which is the point: the fixture was the seventh instance of the AUD-143 shape, and it is the reason the shape is worth searching for in `tests/` as well as `sources/`. `isWaiting` reads the queue rather than one slot, so the tests that wait for a parked caller still work.
    Two test-design rules came out of the hung harnesses and are written into the new tests: a bounded assertion must poll a counter the work writes on its way out, never await the work, because awaiting a parked task cannot time out; and a mutation check must be filtered to the single test under check, because a neighbouring test that *does* await its jobs hangs the whole run instead of failing — measured, during this row's own verification.

**Evidence after.** Commit 07e867b. `RoutingGateTests.everyWaiterOnOneGateIsReleased` passes in 0.068 s with the fixed gate, and fails in 10.066 s with 4 issues against the pre-fix fixture (`releases` reads 1 of 4, then 4 of 5) — the mutation check, run by restoring the old body, measuring, and putting the fix back. `ModelRouterTests` 21 tests green in debug and in release; the stress test's `maxConcurrentGenerations` expectation was removed as this row's own error and the property that actually holds is stated in its place. Full serial debug suite green (1,637 tests across the seven modules, exit 0).

**Commit.** `07e867b`

### AUD-156 — The smoke path installs Playwright unpinned and then executes a CDN browser bundle it never checked

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** installer
- **Location:** `tools/dsh_local.sh:819-836 (ensure_smoke_deps)`
- **Category:** unpinned dependency downloaded and executed, against the script's own pinning rule
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-140 sibling sweep

**Evidence before.** `"$(npm_bin)" install --prefix "$SMOKE_DIR" --no-fund --no-audit playwright` (:826) names no version, while the two other installs in the same file are pinned from constants at the top (`@deepseek-ai/dsh@$DSH_VERSION` :353, `pnpm@$PNPM_VERSION` :394). The file's own header argues the case -- 'a floating version here would turn a working install into a broken one overnight' -- and this is the one place it does not hold. Measured on this host 2026-10-06: `~/.tinytitan/dsh/smoke/node_modules/playwright` is 1.63.0 and `npm view playwright version` is 1.63.0, so what installs is whatever the registry calls latest at the moment someone runs `smoke`, not a version this repository chose. The next line (:833) runs the freshly installed CLI's `install chromium --only-shell`, which pulls a ~150 MB browser bundle from Playwright's CDN into $DSH_ROOT/browsers and launches it: npm's integrity check covers the package against the registry's own metadata, and nothing here covers the browser bundle, so the bytes that get executed on the floating path are decided upstream twice over. Not fixed in AUD-140's commit on purpose: the pin is a choice about which Playwright this project supports, and the only way to learn whether that version still drives the page is a real smoke run, which needs a running server and so falls under the model-run preconditions.

**Fix.** `PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION` is a constant beside `PNPM_VERSION` (`${TINYTITAN_DSH_PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION:-1.63.0}`), the install names it, and the bare `-x .bin/playwright` existence check is replaced by `playwright_installed`, which reads the version out of the package's own manifest and compares it to the pin -- otherwise a leftover from before the pin satisfies the check forever, which is exactly how the floating install stayed working here. Both paths report what they took. The gate is the static rule: `test_the_smoke_playwright_is_pinned_and_checked_against_what_it_got` asserts every npm install in the script carries a version (3, each subtested) and that the pin comparison exists, so a fourth install surface added here fails a gate instead of repeating this one.

**Evidence after.** Measured 2026-10-06. The probe fails on the pre-fix script before it passes: 2 assertions (the unpinned spec, the missing overridable constant). `tools/lint.sh shell` (bash 3.2.57, 27 scripts), `shellcheck` (0.11.0) and `python` (ruff 0.16.7, reached by putting the pipx copy ahead of Homebrew's shadowing 0.16.10 on PATH) pass, and `test_dsh_isolation` is 19/19. The required real run: `tools/dsh_local.sh smoke` against the server on 8080 exits 0 -- `Headless browser already at chromium_headless_shell-1243, which Playwright 1.63.0 chose`, `answer matching /\b42\b/ appeared`, `PASSED`. The first attempt at that run did NOT pass, and the reason is AUD-163: the pin was sound, the page was broken for a different reason -- which is the argument for demanding a real run rather than accepting a static check.

**Commit.** `28a0e7e (fix + gate), closed by the smoke run on a0fae6d`

### AUD-157 — The route writers' byte-equality pin cannot run on a checkout that builds to .build/release, because it probes the arch-triple path the tool never reads

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier B
- **Project:** plugins
- **Location:** `plugins/dsh-tinytitan/test/generate.test.js:30-35, :93-107`
- **Category:** a check that does not run (test harness path vs tool path)
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-130 fix, sibling sweep

**Evidence before.** Found while closing AUD-130, from the suite's own skip line: `the generated block is byte-identical to tools/dsh_route.sh --print` reported `no built TinyTitanServer or tools/dsh_route.sh here` on a host where both exist. `shellComparable` required `existsSync(SHELL_BINARY)` with `SHELL_BINARY = .build/arm64-apple-macosx/release/TinyTitanServer`, while `tools/dsh_route.sh:66-73` resolves `$TINYTITAN_BIN_DIR`, then `$BASE_DIR/.build/release/TinyTitanServer`, then `../bin/` -- never the triple-named directory. The file's own comment (:30-31) claimed 'the test binary may also be the `.build/release` symlink, so both are probed', but the probe was an AND of both paths, so the fallback `TEST_BINARY` could never rescue it. Consequence: on any checkout whose release build is not at the triple path -- which includes a host built through Xcode's `out/Products/Release`, this audit's own machine among them -- the single assertion that the shell writer and the built-in generator produce the same bytes does not run, and nothing else reports that. The audit's plugin suites had therefore been green for weeks on a comparison that had never executed here, including for the `--context`/`--max-tokens` forwarding AUD-130 added in the same batch.

**Fix.** Named the binary the way the tool names it: one `SHELL_BINARY` at `.build/release/TinyTitanServer`, used both by `readCatalog` and by the probe, so the two sides of the comparison read the same file and the assertion is about the writers rather than about discovery; the triple path and the `TEST_BINARY` alias are gone. Scrubbed `TINYTITAN_BIN_DIR` from the environment `shellBlock` passes to the tool, next to the `TINYTITAN_CATALOG_JSON`/`_MODELS_DIR`/`_PORT`/`_SERVER` names already removed: it outranks the checkout path in the tool's own order (:66-67), so an ambient one -- which is exactly what the installer's launcher sets -- would make the test compare two different builds and call the difference a writer bug. The skip line now prints the path it looked for, so a genuine skip says what is missing instead of guessing. Not fixed by creating the triple directory: that would manufacture the condition the test asks about rather than ask the right question, and `tools/lint.sh arch-path` exists to keep hardcoded triples out of build paths. Scope note found on the way, and left alone deliberately: the two sides read different environment names for the same job. The shell tool honours `TINYTITAN_BIN_DIR` and `TINYTITAN_DEFAULT_PORT`, the JS side honours `TINYTITAN_SERVER`, `TINYTITAN_REASONING` and now `TINYTITAN_CONTEXT`/`TINYTITAN_MAX_TOKENS`, and none of the six names is read by both except `TINYTITAN_PORT` and `TINYTITAN_MODELS_DIR`. That is a documentation shape rather than a defect -- the plugin always forwards what it resolved as explicit flags, so the effective route is the same whichever side runs -- and unifying the names would change what an existing installation means, which is the user's call, not a sweep's. Recorded here so the next reader does not rediscover it as a bug.

**Evidence after.** Before, on this host: `npm test` -> 137 tests / 136 pass / 1 skipped, the skip being the byte-equality pin, with `.build/release -> out/Products/Release` and a real `TinyTitanServer` behind it. After ee72cbb: 137 / 137 pass / **0 skipped**, the pin taking 177.6 ms against the installed catalog (2 x qwen3.8-flash-next 125B-A6B 4-bit), so the two writers were compared for real -- including the narrowed case, which the test already covered (`--context 131072 --max-tokens 8192` versus `generateBlock(...)`). Independent hand check before the fix, same numbers: the tool's `--print` and the generator's block were 41 lines each and `cmp` exit 0, and `--print` with neither flag printed `defaultContextWindow: 262144` / `defaultMaxTokens: 32768`. Mutation check that the pin bites: `defaultContextWindow: ${context}` -> `${context + 1}` in src/generate.js:218 fails `the generated block is byte-identical to tools/dsh_route.sh --print` plus four siblings (14 pass / 5 fail); reverting returns 19/19. A first attempt at that mutation was vacuous -- the pattern omitted the six spaces inside the template literal, matched nothing, and reported 19/19 as if it were evidence -- which is why the check is reported with the grep line that proves the file changed. `tools/lint.sh javascript` ok for both packages (node v26.10.0, eslint 10.11.0, prettier 3.9.9) after `npm run format`.

**Commit.** `ee72cbb`

### AUD-159 — RELEASE.md requires `lipo -archs <binary>` to report exactly `arm64` and nothing in the release path ever runs lipo; the only arm64 claim in a shipped artifact is its filename

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier B
- **Project:** release
- **Location:** `RELEASE.md:26-31 (rule 2), tools/release.sh:47-48,310,369-377, tools/build_library.sh:97`
- **Category:** unenforced documented standard (missing gate)
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-151 fix, sibling sweep (asking which other written standards are carried by habit alone)

**Evidence before.** RELEASE.md rule 2 is stated twice, in the non-negotiables of AGENTS.md and in full in the release standard: 'Build native `arm64` ... Never `--arch x86_64`, never `ARCHS=arm64 x86_64`, and never `lipo -create`' and '**Assert it** - `lipo -archs <binary>` must report exactly `arm64`. A build that silently produced a fat binary is a release defect, not a build option.' `grep -rn lipo tools/` returns **nothing**: the word appears in this repository's tooling only inside a comment in .github/workflows/codeql.yml:89. What the release path does check is names, not bytes - `tools/release.sh:47-48` builds the stage and archive paths as `tinytitan-$VERSION-macos-arm64.tar.gz`, :310 copies resource bundles, :369-377 asserts the library archive carries `libTinyTitanLib.a`, `libTinyTitanLib.dylib`, the module and the Metal bundle by *member name* (`tar tzf | grep -q`), and `tools/build_library.sh:97` asserts the dylib's install name with `otool -D`. An x86_64-only or fat Mach-O staged under those names would pass every one of them: the arch is asserted nowhere in `tools/release.sh`, nowhere in `tools/build_library.sh`, and nowhere in CI (which builds and tests, and does not stage a release artifact). Measured on the current tree, the claim happens to hold - `lipo -archs` on `.build/release/TinyTitanCLI`, `.build/release/TinyTitanServer` and `.build/release/libTinyTitanLib.a` each report exactly `arm64` - which is the point: the promise is currently true because of how SwiftPM was invoked, and nothing would notice the day it is not. The consequence of a miss is not cosmetic: the artifact is downloaded by name as 'prebuilt binaries (macOS, Apple Silicon / arm64)' (release.sh:316), Rosetta would hide an x86_64 slice on this host, and the sha256 published in the release notes would certify the wrong bytes for the platform the release exists to serve.

**Fix.** The assertion now runs inside the release path, in one implementation with three call sites. `tools/assert-arch.sh` (new, 98 lines) is sourced, not copied: it is a library of `assert_arm64_dir` / `assert_arm64_archive` and, when invoked directly, a CLI that dispatches on file shape (single file by magic, directory, archive). Detection is by first-four-bytes magic against the full Mach-O set - thin 32/64 in either byte order, fat 32/64, and `!<arch>` - chosen after measuring that `lipo -archs` on a `.swiftmodule` exits 1 with `cannot mmap() ... errno=22`, so a name- or extension-based scan would have made the gate's own module its first false positive, while a `.a` *is* readable and is therefore in scope rather than a hole. Each candidate must report exactly `arm64`; the two failure messages are distinct by design ('reports arches ...' vs 'lipo cannot read ...'). Call sites: `release.sh` asserts the unpacked engine archive and the unpacked library archive, each **before** that archive's `shasum`, so no checksum is ever taken over unasserted bytes; `build_library.sh` asserts its staging directory, which is the standalone operator path that never goes through `release.sh`; CI asserts the four built products (new step, 'The arm64 promise (RELEASE.md rule 2)'). A stage containing no Mach-O dies rather than passing vacuously. Docs: RELEASE.md §1.2.2 records why the check must be executed rather than recited, part 2's Artifacts bullet names the script and the three places it runs, and `docs/release-process.md` step 4/5 describe the order the checks now run in.

**Evidence after.** Proven by mutation, not by a green run. `docs/audit-2026-10-06/AUD-159-arch-probe.sh` (new, committed) extracts `release.sh`'s own stage -> package -> checksum lines (74 lines) and runs them unmodified: with the real products it asserts then checksums; with `/usr/bin/lipo` (fat) planted as TinyTitanCLI it dies and **no .sha256 exists**; restoring the real binary passes again. The sibling arm does the same for the missing membership loop: without it a three-binary archive gets a checksum, with it TinyTitanBench is named and the checksum refused. Arming the gate directly: engine archive 4 Mach-O each exactly arm64, library archive 2 (its 29 .swiftmodule bitcode files are skipped, as measured), then fat -> "reports arches 'x86_64 arm64e arm64e.x1'", thinned x86_64 -> "'x86_64'", thinned arm64e -> 'arm64e', 16-byte file with cffaedfe magic -> 'lipo cannot read ... lipo: not a mach-o', text-only stage -> 'nothing executable was staged'. CLI mode matches on a file, a directory, an archive, and refuses `release.sh` itself ('not a Mach-O, an archive or a directory'). 19/19 arms behave under bash 5.3.20 **and** under /bin/bash 3.2.57 (rc=0 both). Gates: `tools/lint.sh shellcheck` ok (0.11.0, 27 scripts), `tools/lint.sh shell` ok (system bash 3.2.57, 27 scripts) - the SC1090 on the runtime-derived `source` is closed with `# shellcheck source=/dev/null`, which was verified to be the directive doing the work, not a silently ignored one.

Two things this batch did NOT confirm, stated rather than smoothed over: (1) a full `tools/release.sh --dry-run` is **not checked** - its precondition chain demands the tag be pushed, and 'do not push yet' is in force, so call-site reachability is proven on the script's own extracted lines instead of on a whole run. (2) The row's prepared expectation asked for the **demo binary** in the library stage; measured, there is none - `tools/build_library.sh` ships `demo/main.swift` plus `build-static.sh` and `build-dynamic.sh`, source and scripts only. The library archive's 2 Mach-O are the .a and the .dylib, so the guard covers what actually ships, and the expectation was wrong, not the fix.

Sibling defect found and fixed in the same batch (5a195d8): the engine archive had no per-product membership assertion. `release.sh` runs `set -uo pipefail` without errexit, so a failing `cp` is silent, and the stage loop's `[ -x "$BIN/$p" ]` is true for a *directory*, which `cp` then skips with 'is a directory (not copied)'. A release could therefore ship three binaries under a name promising four - and the new arch count would have reported '3 Mach-O artifacts' as if that were the specification. The loop now requires each of the four products by name inside the tar, which is what makes the count mean four rather than 'whatever arrived'.

**Commit.** `f485fef, 5a195d8, 4dea3b3`

### AUD-161 — A quantized weight width outside [4, 8] is accepted by the CPU snapshot reader, and the one place that did route a 6-bit width could only abort the process

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier B
- **Project:** engine
- **Location:** `sources/TinyTitan/CPUEngine/AffineSnapshot.swift:176-192, sources/TinyTitan/Kernels/MoE/SharedExpertInt4.swift:110-140, sources/TinyTitan/Kernels/MoE/SharedExpertAffineQuant.swift (deleted), sources/TinyTitanFormat/SSDAIManifestV1.swift:248-258 (guard, previously untested)`
- **Category:** input validation at a trust boundary (width reaches kernel arithmetic)
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-159 fix, sibling sweep (which other numbers read from a file reach arithmetic unasked?)

**Evidence before.** The width is not a preference. Kernels derive their addressing from it: `AffineQuant`/`SlotGEMV`/`MoE`/`MPPPrefillInt4QMM`/`PrefillGroupedRoutedMoE`/`PrefillPrimitives`/`PrefillFinalRowHead` all carry `precondition([4, 8].contains(weightBits))` (AffineQuant.swift:48 and :131, SlotGEMV.swift:30-32, MoE.swift:134, MPPPrefillInt4QMM.swift:34, PrefillGroupedRoutedMoE.swift:208, PrefillPrimitives.swift:8 and :98, PrefillFinalRowHead.swift:14); the CPU path either dies on purpose (`CPUTensorOps.swift:154` `preconditionFailure("no CPU kernel for \(matrix.bits)-bit weights")`) or divides by it in silence (`CPUQwen35+Quant.swift:16` `let lanes = 32 / matrix.bits` -- at 6 bits that is 5 lanes, and the same bytes unpack to plausible nonsense). Measured rather than argued: a throwaway test constructing `AffineQuantGEMV` at 6 bits exited with signal 5 on `TinyTitan/AffineQuant.swift:48: Precondition failed`; the probe was then deleted.
Per route: (1) GPU manifest -- already gated twice: a slot width is refused at manifest read (`ManifestReader.validateQuant`, ManifestReader.swift:256-265) and a per-tensor override is refused while decoding (`SSDAIManifestQuantV1.init(from:)`, SSDAIManifestV1.swift:248-258). **This part of the report was not true**: my first hypothesis was that overrides were ungated on the GPU route; a `Model.validateOverrideWidths` gate was written against that hypothesis, the decoder guard was then found, and both edits were fully reverted -- the honest residue is that a real guard had **no test**: `grep -rnE "quant override for|supportedWeightBits|bits; supported" tests/` returned nothing. (2) CPU snapshot (`config.json`) -- the live hole. `AffineSnapshot` read `quantization.bits` and every per-tensor override with `as? Int` casts and no range check at any point before the width reached `dequantize` and the GEMV dispatch. (3) The CPU `.ssdai` route shares the gated decoder. (4) `SharedExpertAffineQuant.swift` (73 lines) was a 6-bit-only composition whose **single** construction site passed `weightBits: 6` into `AffineQuantGEMV`, which asserts [4, 8] -- so `SharedExpertInt4`'s `case 6:` arm could not produce output or an error, only a trap; 6-bit is a withdrawn format per AGENTS.md, so the arm was dead code whose only reachable behaviour was a crash.

**Fix.** The gate moved to where the width is read, and the dead arm was deleted. `AffineSnapshot.validateWidths(baseBits:widths:)` (new, sources/TinyTitan/CPUEngine/AffineSnapshot.swift) checks the declared base width **and** every per-tensor override -- sorted, so the refusal is deterministic -- and throws `SafeTensorsFile.Failure.malformed("... declares N-bit weights. The CPU kernels implement 4 and 8 only, so this snapshot cannot be read correctly -- not as a reference and not as output.")`. It is called from the safetensors/`config.json` initializer only; the `.ssdai` initializer documents why it does not need it (the decoder already refused), rather than adding a second, differently-worded check of the same fact. `SharedExpertAffineQuant.swift` is deleted and `SharedExpertInt4` loses its `.affine` case, its `case 6:` and the encode arm, leaving `default: throw SharedExpertError.unsupportedWeightBits(weightBits)` -- an error, naming the width, instead of a trap. The comment at the switch records which two guards keep an unsupported width from ever arriving. Tests: `tests/TinyTitan/Kernels/MoE/SharedExpertRuntimeTests.swift` (new) pins 4 and 8 building and 6/3/16/0/32 throwing with the width both in the case payload and in `error.description`; `ManifestReaderTests` gains the first test of the pre-existing override decode guard, at 6/3/16/2 bits, asserting the message names the tensor stem; `CPUEngineTests` gains base-width and override-width arms through the real `AffineSnapshot(directory:)` loader.

**Evidence after.** Corrections first: the row's own first hypothesis (GPU per-tensor overrides ungated) was **not true**, and the code written for it was reverted before commit -- `git status` on `Model+Validation.swift` and `Model+SchemaValidation.swift` is clean, which is the evidence that it is reverted and not merely described as so.
The trap claim is measured: signal 5 with `TinyTitan/AffineQuant.swift:48: Precondition failed` from a throwaway test, not an assertion about preconditions.
Every new assertion was mutation-checked, reverted, and re-verified green. M1 -- delete the `AffineSnapshot.validateWidths` call site: exactly 4 issues in `CPUEngineTests` (34 pass after restoring). ### AUD-164 — The CPU snapshot opens every shard name it reads out of the model index with no containment and no O_NOFOLLOW, while three sibling loaders fence the same contract

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** engine
- **Location:** `sources/TinyTitan/CPUEngine/AffineSnapshot.swift:205 (the fenced open loop, formerly an unguarded appendPathComponent), sources/TinyTitan/CPUEngine/SafeTensors.swift:80 (the O_NOFOLLOW opener)`
- **Category:** trusting manifest content: the boundary fenced everywhere else is unfenced on one path
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** the L4 security sweep over names and bytes that come from outside this process

**Evidence before.** An installed model directory can arrive copied off another machine, so an index's `weight_map` values are external input, not a list this process wrote. The CPU loader turned each one straight into `directory.appendingPathComponent(file)` and handed the URL to `SafeTensorsFile(url:)`, whose opener was a plain `open(O_RDONLY)`: no canonicalisation, so `../../...` resolved out of the snapshot, and no `O_NOFOLLOW`, so a symlink at a plausible shard name mapped a file outside the directory into the engine's address space. `SSDAIModelDirectory` already fences both halves (a non-canonical name is refused, every component opens `O_NOFOLLOW` relative to the directory's own descriptor), `LocalSnapshotLoader` fences the same contract for the other engine, and the `.ssdai` path fences it again -- three siblings and one hole. The hole is on the CPU path, which is the one a user reaches for when the GPU path will not fit.

**Fix.** The shard loop opens through `SSDAIModelDirectory(rootURL:)` the way its siblings do, so containment is checked per name and every component opens relative to the snapshot's own descriptor. `SafeTensorsFile` gains an init that adopts an already-open descriptor, because opening by name and then re-opening by URL is a TOCTOU: the bytes mapped must be the bytes that were checked. The URL init now sets `O_NOFOLLOW` itself, so the fence lives in the opener and a caller cannot forget it.

**Evidence after.** Measured 2026-10-06 during the L4 pass. 4 tests in `tests/TinyTitan/CPUEngine/CPUEngineTests.swift`: `aShardNameThatEscapesTheSnapshotIsRefused`, `aSymlinkedShardIsRefusedRatherThanMapped`, `aSymlinkedURLIsRefusedByTheOpener`, and AUD-165's bound test. Against the pre-fix sources all four fail with `an error was expected but none was thrown`, so each binds to the fence rather than to the fixture. The full CPU suite is 38 tests in 2 suites, passed, re-run after the fix commits. NOT covered as filed: `AffineSnapshot.swift` was at exactly 500 physical lines, the `file-length` ceiling with no headroom, so the next change to the file had to split it along a seam first. That is what 75501ed did: the two loaders and `fullAttentionInterval(of:)` moved to `AffineSnapshot+Loading.swift` as pure code motion, 231 added lines against 219 removed -- the difference is the new file's `import Foundation`, its header and the extension brace.

**Commit.** `1745078`

### AUD-165 — The second metadata read in the same initializer is still an uncapped whole-file Data(contentsOf:), the shape AUD-150 closed for the other seven

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** engine
- **Location:** `sources/TinyTitan/CPUEngine/AffineSnapshot.swift:191 (the index read, now through BoundedMetadataRead)`
- **Category:** read-then-check: a bound applied after the allocation bounds the decision, not the memory
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** following AUD-150's rule to every metadata read rather than only the seven it named

**Evidence before.** AUD-150 moved seven metadata reads onto `BoundedMetadataRead`, which `fstat`s the descriptor and refuses before allocating. This one survived in the same initializer that reads the manifest sitting beside it: `JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(contentsOf: indexURL))`. The file's name comes from the directory being loaded, so a sparse index allocates the whole thing first and only then fails to parse. AUD-150 measured the identical shape on a 2 GiB sparse file: 0.350 s and +2,049 MB of `phys_footprint` on a 24 GB Mac.

**Fix.** The index read goes through `BoundedMetadataRead.read(fileAt:maxBytes:)` with the same `maxBytes` the sibling manifest read in this initializer already carries, so the bound is the one the loader already declares rather than a number invented here.

**Evidence after.** Measured 2026-10-06. `anOversizedIndexIsRefusedByTheBoundNotByTheParse` asserts both halves: that it is refused, and that the refusal names the bound rather than a JSON error -- a parse failure would satisfy a test that only checked for an error, and would mean the bound was never what stopped it. Runs green in the same 38-test CPU suite.

**Commit.** `1745078`

### AUD-166 — The gate that hunts unbounded reads matches one physical line, so it printed ok over the wrapped call AUD-165 is -- and it prints ok when its own walk found no files

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** lint-gates
- **Location:** `tools/lint.sh:119 (unbounded_read_hits), tools/lint.sh:155 (check_unbounded_metadata_read)`
- **Category:** a gate that cannot see the defect it exists to catch, and cannot see whether it ran
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** running the gate over AUD-165's site instead of trusting its ok

**Evidence before.** `unbounded-read` tested `/(Data|String)\(contentsOf:/` against each line as it came from `readlines()`. `swift-format` wraps a call whose arguments do not fit, which is exactly what AUD-165's read looked like -- `Data(` on one line, `contentsOf: url)` on the next -- so the gate reported ok over the one site it had been asked to find. Second hole in the same function: `Dir.glob` returning nothing raised nothing, so an empty scan printed ok over the whole tree. That is the AUD-104 defect -- a gate that did not run reading as a pass -- inside the gate that hunts unbounded reads.

**Fix.** The matcher joins a continuation-line window before testing, so a wrapped call is one match. The walker raises `no Swift files under <root>` on an empty root, and the shell side turns a failed walk into a FAIL with the reason printed instead of falling through to ok.

**Evidence after.** Measured 2026-10-06 on current code, both halves: the same synthetic wrapped read was placed under `sources/`, the pre-fix gate restored from 766cb27^ exited 0 printing `ok`, and the fixed gate exited 1 with `FAIL: unbounded whole-file read without a 'lint:allow-unbounded-read <reason>' comment above it` naming file and line; the probe file was removed and the clean tree is ok again, exit 0. Joining the lines surfaced one real site the old grep never saw: `sources/TinyTitanCLI/Run.swift:203`, the `--messages-file` read mapped `.mappedIfSafe`, which carries the audited exemption because the bytes are a file the operator named and the mapping is the point of the read.

### AUD-167 — POST /v1/models/unload has no browser-form gate, so a form POST from any LAN page can reach the route that unloads the resident model

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** server
- **Location:** `sources/TinyTitanServer/Core/HTTPServerHandler+Routes.swift:139 (the guard), :51 (notAForm)`
- **Category:** half-covered guard: five mutating routes check the content type and the sixth does not
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** enumerating which routes the AUD-147 Origin/content-type guards actually reach

**Evidence before.** `/v1/models/unload` read its body through the absent-content-type-tolerant helper rather than the gated path, so an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or `multipart/form-data` POST -- what a browser sends from a plain `<form>` with no preflight to answer for it -- reached the route whose only effect is to drop the loaded model. The other five mutating JSON routes all carry the gate. The helper could not simply be swapped: its absent-header permissiveness is the CLI's contract, which is the AUD-132 lesson, so the route needed the guard rather than a stricter body reader. Nothing in the suite had ever sent a non-JSON content type to any of the five that do carry the gate, so the missing sixth had no test to fail and the guard was pinned only by memory.

**Fix.** `notAForm` is computed once at the top of the route table and the unload case guards on it, answering 415 through the same `writeUnsupportedMediaType` the other five use, so the envelope stays per-surface instead of inventing a new error shape.

**Evidence after.** Measured 2026-10-06. `unloadRefusesABrowserFormPost` drives three form encodings at the live route and asserts 415 and that the body does not say `unloaded`. `everyJsonRouteRefusesANonJsonContentType` pins the gate on all five gated routes at once and checks the two surfaces apart because they answer apart: the OpenAI envelope carries `unsupported_media_type` and the Anthropic one is `invalid_request_error` with no code field at all -- the first draft read that as a missing gate until it printed the body. The encoder escapes the slash in `application/json`, so the message assertion stops before it. `HTTPServerTests` is 22/22 passed.

**Commit.** `a087c90`

### AUD-169 — The route validator prints model ids it reads off a running server straight into the settings block, where both sibling writers validate the same field

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** python-tooling
- **Location:** `tools/dsh_route.sh (the --from-server served-id block)`
- **Category:** trusting an id read from the network on one writer and validating it on two
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** comparing the three writers of the same settings block against each other

**Evidence before.** `--from-server` asks a live server for `/v1/models` and writes each id verbatim into the YAML block it emits. The catalogue parser refuses an empty or multi-line field and the plugin writer runs the same validator over its own input; this path asked neither question, on the theory that a running server only names real models. An id carrying a newline became two rows in the block, and one carrying YAML punctuation changed what the block declares rather than what it names. The failure was also invisible: the python check raised into a command substitution whose stderr was not the launcher's, so the operator saw `listed no models` instead of the reason.

**Fix.** Every served id must match `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` before anything is printed, the refusal captures the validator's stderr and passes it to `die`, and nothing is emitted unless the whole listing passes -- so a refusal leaves the array empty and the existing empty-listing error still fires.

**Evidence after.** Measured 2026-10-06. 4 tests in `benchmark/test_dsh_route.py` (`ServedIdTests`) drive a real `ThreadingHTTPServer` on 127.0.0.1 port 0 rather than a stub, because the claim is what the shell does with a live answer: plain ids reach the block, an id with a newline is refused, an id with YAML punctuation is refused, and one bad id refuses the whole listing. Suite: 17 passed including the 4 new. `tools/lint.sh shell` and `shellcheck` clean, and the loop is a `while read` rather than `mapfile` because /bin/bash on a factory Mac is 3.2.

**Commit.** `a5ee765`

### AUD-172 — Neither settings-file route writer repoints agent-default-model, so a profile without a settings service gets the stale-default failure AUD-163 closed

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** plugin
- **Location:** `plugins/dsh-tinytitan/src/route.js:77 (registerRoute), plugins/dsh-tinytitan/src/generate.js:476 (repairDefaultModelSettings)`
- **Category:** stale configuration reference after a refresh
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** the L6 closure sweep, which re-read every row's NOT-covered sentence against the current code rather than trusting it

**Evidence before.** AUD-163's own caveat named this branch and said it was not covered: "the pre-0.2.0 file path (`generateRoute`/`writeRouteSettings`, reached when a harness has no settings service) still writes only `llm-pi-ai` and inherits the same stale-default defect." Checked, and live. `index.js` picks the writer by whether the profile composes a settings service (:122 `legacy = registerRoute`, called at :212 via `ctx.inject(["settings"], ...)`), and on a profile that answers no `settings` the legacy writer runs instead. Both of its halves refresh only the route: the shell branch executes `tools/dsh_route.sh --write`, and `generateRoute`/`writeRouteSettings` rewrite the `llm-pi-ai` section. Nothing on that path ever read `agent-default-model`. Consequence, the same as AUD-163's: after the operator changed which model is installed the refresh updated the picker, the window showed the live model, every turn went out naming the dead id and came back `pi-ai provider "tinytitan" has no configured model <id>` / `UNKNOWN_MODEL`, and the profile looked correctly configured the whole time. `ensureDefaultModel` -- the repair -- was reachable only from `applyRouteThroughSettings`, i.e. only on the branch the pinned harness takes, which is why 144 green tests never saw the other one.

**Fix.** The repair moved out of the service call and next to both file writes. `applyDefaultModelToSettings` is the pure half: it reads the served ids back out of the `llm-pi-ai` block in the file (`servedIdsInLines`), which is what the writer just wrote, so one implementation works after either the shell tool or the built-in generator refreshed it; it returns `repaired`/`kept`/`skipped` with the reason, and rewrites only the one `model:` line, to the first served id. `repairDefaultModelSettings` is the file half and shares the new `replaceSettingsFile` with `writeRouteSettings`, so a refresh and a repair cannot disagree about whether a no-op makes a `.bak-*`; its stamp carries a `-default` suffix so its backup of the same file cannot clobber the route write's backup. `registerRoute` calls it through `repairDefaultAfterWrite` after each of the two success branches and adds the outcome to the result as `defaultModel`, the field the service branch already returns. The rule stays as narrow as AUD-163's, for the stated reason: this edits somebody else's profile, so a default naming a served model is a choice, a default belonging to another provider is a choice, and a default that was never set is `dsh_local.sh`'s job -- only a reference this repository wrote and can prove dead is rewritten. A repair failure never fails the refresh: the route is already on disk and turning `written` into `failed` would push the caller down the "leaving the route as it is" path over a smaller, separate defect, so the reason goes to the log.

**Evidence after.** Measured 2026-10-06. Probe first, on the pre-fix sources: a standalone driver of `registerRoute`'s script branch against a profile whose route serves `alpha_4-Bit` and whose default names `gone_4-Bit`, run with `src/generate.js` and `src/route.js` restored from `git show HEAD:` (backed up to /tmp first, then put back and confirmed by `git diff`) -- it fails with `AssertionError: no default repair ran on the file branch / actual undefined, expected 'repaired'`, exit 1. The same driver passes on the fixed sources. 10 unit and integration tests added: the pure rule over all six outcomes, the block found on either side of the route (the scan stops at the next column-0 key, so a default below `llm-pi-ai:` must be read as carefully as one above), the write-once-and-back-up and no-op-makes-no-backup behaviour over a real file, both writers' integration (built-in generator, and the script branch with an injected `run`), and `chmod 0o000` on the settings file to show a repair that cannot write still returns `written` with the reason logged. Suites after: dsh-tinytitan `npm test` 154 passed / 0 failed (was 144), `tools/lint.sh javascript` ok on the pinned eslint 10.11.0 / prettier 3.9.9 -- it failed once on an unused binding in the new tests before it passed, so the gate is live. NOT covered: the shell branch's repair is pinned against an injected `run`, so it proves what `registerRoute` does with the file after the tool exits, not that `dsh_route.sh` wrote a valid block -- that half is AUD-157's checkout-tool comparison.

**Commit.** `7ce0a85`

### AUD-176 — The CPU serving path accepts `seed`, `presence_penalty` and `repetition_penalty`, applies none of them, and is the engine meant to check the GPU path with

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** engine
- **Location:** `sources/TinyTitanServer/Core/CPUModelBackend.swift:189-195 (the sampler built from the config) and sources/TinyTitan/CPUEngine/CPUSampler.swift:15-31 (the shape it could hold)`
- **Category:** documented API accepted then dropped on one of two engines, so the same request answers differently with nothing said
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** the L7/section-5 pass, looking for a second implementation of generation that had drifted from the first -- AGENTS rule 2 says a front end that reimplements sampling is drift, and here it had

**Evidence before.** The validator is shared: `OpenAIRequestValidator.swift:194-195,276-280` puts `presencePenalty`, `repetitionPenalty` and `seed` on one `GenerationConfig` for every entry, GPU or CPU. The GPU sampler reads all three -- `Runtime/Generation/Sampler.swift:83-93` applies both penalties before the kernel sees the row, and `:294-299` `seedFor(config:position:)` honours `config.seed` -- while the CPU backend at 7cee919's parent built `CPUSampler(temperature:topP:topK:seed:)` from a `CPUSampler` struct that has no penalty fields at all, and set the seed with `configuration.temperature > 0 ? nil : 0`. `grep -n 'presencePenalty|repetitionPenalty|\.seed'` over the whole backend returned nothing. The consequence is not only a request that asks for `presence_penalty: 1.5` and does not get it -- it is a model row that publishes it: `GenerationDefaults.qwen38Instruct` carries `presencePenalty: 1.5` (`SamplerTypes.swift:55-57`), so serving a non-thinking Qwen3.8 request on CPU silently removes a penalty the checkpoint specifies. And this engine exists to be an independent reference for the GPU one (`docs/plan-cpu-side-engine.md`), so a dropped penalty is the comparison disagreeing for a reason that is in neither model. No document said the CPU path was penalty-free, and `--cpu` is a usage-text flag (`ServerArguments+Usage.swift:105`), not a debug switch. Nothing in `tests/` covered the sampled CPU path at all: `CPUModelBackendTests` generated once, at `temperature: 0`.

**Fix.** `CPUSampler` carries both penalties and applies them the way the GPU sampler does, minus its softcap branch because this engine has no softcap: a distinct id in the history is divided by the repetition factor while its logit is positive and multiplied while negative, then has the presence penalty subtracted -- before the argmax, so greedy respects them too, as the GPU's greedy does. An id outside the row is skipped rather than trapping. The backend seeds the history with the prompt ids and appends each produced token, because the prompt is in the model's context and the GPU caller passes the same thing, and it takes the request's seed instead of deriving one from the temperature. The config-to-sampler mapping became `CPUModelBackend.cpuSampler(for:)` so the wiring is testable without a model; an absent seed now stays absent rather than folding into 0, which is the generator's own fixed state and would have made every unseeded request draw the same sequence. A stale inverted comment on `CPUSampler.seed` (it claimed nil was the deterministic case) is corrected, and `docs/plan-cpu-side-engine.md`'s "generation is greedy, deliberately" is given the sentence that says what it now means.

**Evidence after.** Measured 2026-10-07 on commit 7cee919. Five new tests. Four in `tests/TinyTitan/CPUEngine/CPUEngineTests.swift` on the sampler: presence takes a seen token out of contention under greedy, and the same request with an empty history still picks it; repetition scales by sign in both directions (positive 3 -> 1.5 under 2.5, negative -2 -> -4 under -2.5) which is the case an implementation that always divides fails; both penalties at their defaults change nothing; a history id of 999 or -3 costs a token, not the process. One in `tests/TinyTitanServer/CPUModelBackendTests.swift` on the wiring: all six fields arrive at the sampler and an absent seed is nil, not 0. Two mutation probes, each restored and verified by checksum: deleting the `presencePenalty:` line from the factory fails the wiring test with 1 issue; replacing the penalty loop's source with an empty set fails the presence and repetition tests with 3 issues while the neutral-defaults and out-of-range tests pass -- those two are deliberate counter-tests, they must hold on both trees. Full `swift test --no-parallel`: exit 0, 1687 tests in 251 suites passed against 1682 before, so the five new ones ran; swift-format, swiftlint --strict, file-length (largest 496) and docs (83 documents, 17 gates) clean. NOT covered: no live-model run of the fixed CPU path -- the golden baseline is a GPU target, `models/` holds only the two 125B installs, and a `TinyTitanServer` was serving one of them throughout, which the model-run preconditions forbid stopping or duplicating. Also NOT covered, and deliberately not changed: the two engines' nucleus is measured over different supports -- this one normalises inside the top-k subset, `logit.metal:576-581` accumulates over the whole row -- so `top_k` with `top_p` is not the same function on both. Fixing that is a numerics decision for the user, not a fence, and it is written into `docs/plan-cpu-side-engine.md` as an open question instead of being quietly resolved. The `minP` field is not dropped here: a non-zero value is already refused by `validate`, which is the pattern this row should have followed.

**Commit.** `7cee919`

### AUD-178 — `--draft-head` and `--share-ngram-table` are accepted on three routes that never read them, including the one that then downloads 36.9 GB of the wrong model

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** repack
- **Location:** `sources/TinyTitanRepack/Command/main.swift:36-37,71-75,224-225 (the flags, the parse cases, and the one place they were forwarded)`
- **Category:** documented-by-error-message CLI flags silently dropped on every path except the one that implements them
- **Status:** DONE

**Evidence before.** `Arguments` carries `draftHead` and `shareNgramTable` (`main.swift:36-37`), the parse loop sets both on any invocation (`:71-75`), and they are forwarded at exactly one site: `LocalSnapshotRepackOptions(draftHead:shareNgramTable:)` inside `if let input = arguments.inputSnapshot` at `:224-225`. Every other route builds something else: the download route calls `SupportedModelSource.installOptions(outputDirectory:overwrite:token:resume:)` (`Core/Remote/SupportedModelSource.swift:19-25`), which has no parameter for either; `--discard-partial` returns at `:112` before the import branch; `--verify-install` builds `VerifyInstallOptions(inputSSDAI:)`. The local branch's own guard at `:129-132` lists both flags as accepted but only checks the reverse direction -- that a local import is not mixed with `--model`, `--resume`, `--verify-install` or `--input-ssdai` -- so nothing anywhere required `--input-snapshot`. ### AUD-179 — `repetition_penalty` below one is accepted by the wire, refused mid-request by one backend and answered backwards by the other

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** server
- **Location:** `sources/TinyTitanLib/OpenAIRequestValidator.swift:194-199 (the wire's bound) against sources/TinyTitan/Runtime/Generation/SamplerTypes.swift:165-168 (the engine's)`
- **Category:** boundary range wider than the engine's, so a client error becomes a 500 -- or an inverted penalty
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** the L7/§5 facade hunt, tracing each sampling field from the wire to the kernel. --repetition-penalty's own comment (sources/TinyTitanCLI/Args.swift:300-306) says the CLI must not accept a configuration every other front end rejects; the wire was that other front end, and it did

**Evidence before.** The wire accepted repetitionPenalty > 0 (OpenAIRequestValidator.swift:194-195); the engine requires isFinite, >= 1 and throws GeneratorError.invalidGenerationConfig (SamplerTypes.swift:165-168, whose comment already records why: below one the pass rewards repetition instead of penalising it). GenerationConfig.validate() is called on the GPU route -- ServerModelSession+Generation.swift:250 then Runtime/Generation/RawCompletion.swift:134 -- so a request carrying repetition_penalty 0.5 passed validation and then threw before prefill, and HTTPServerHandler+Streaming.swift:111-117 maps a non-ServerRequestError to .internalServerError with "generation failed; see TinyTitanServer stderr": a client mistake as a 500, and on a stream after the 200 and the assistant chunk were already sent. The CPU route reaches no validate at all -- grep -n validate over CPUModelBackend.swift returns nothing -- so the same request ran, and CPUSampler.applyPenalties (CPUSampler.swift:131-133) divides a positive logit by 0.5 and multiplies a negative one by it, which rewards the repeated token. Neither end was pinned: no test asserted the wire bound, and SampleTopK64Tests.swift:13-60 exercises validate() for defaults, minP and topK/topP but never for repetitionPenalty.

**Fix.** The boundary that can answer 400 now applies the engine's bound: guard repetitionPenalty >= 1, refused as invalid_request_error with param repetition_penalty and the reason in the message, so one request gets one answer on both engines and no penalty is ever served inverted.

**Evidence after.** RED first, on the unmodified tree: the new test recorded failure -> nil at OpenAIValidationTests.swift:459, i.e. the validator accepted 0.5 (exit 1, 1 issue). GREEN after the guard: Test run with 37 tests in 3 suites passed, exit 0. The suite now asserts both halves -- 0.5 refused, and that whatever the wire accepts survives generationConfig.validate(), which is the anti-drift assertion. Full suite 1696 tests in 252 suites, exit 0, 0 issues (was 1695/251); all 17 tools/lint.sh gates exit 0. Sibling sweep: the CLI and the engine already fenced this field; the Anthropic and Responses mappers send repetitionPenalty nil (AnthropicMapper.swift:448, ResponsesAPIMapper.swift:314), which defaults to 1; the facade's raw path (Session.swift:156-168) bypasses the validator but reaches the engine's validate() before prefill and rethrows it typed at :184-191, so it refuses late rather than wrongly. Residual, not fixed here: CPUModelBackend still runs no GenerationConfig.validate(). Unreachable from the wire now that every field's bound matches, but a future internal GenerationConfig could still be served by one engine and refused by the other.

### AUD-182 — The fleet manager reports success for any 200 answer: an ack with no `ok` field, a string `ok`, or a proxy's HTML page all print `ok`, and a peer that genuinely refuses exits 0 while `prompt` exits 1 for the same event

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier B
- **Project:** fleet
- **Location:** `sources/TinyTitanFleet/Core/FleetClient.swift:209-212 (the `?? true` in ack()), sources/TinyTitanFleet/Command/main.swift:139-141 (report), :309-331 (the three arms that used it)`
- **Category:** integrity / fail-open check, error swallowed into a success answer
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** L3 line-level pass over the fleet client's response handling, from the AUD-170 sibling sweep of FleetClient

**Evidence before.** Verified against the code and then against the shipped binary before filing. `FleetClient.ack()` decoded the body with `try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(...) as? [String: Any]` and answered `ok: (object?["ok"] as? Bool) ?? true`, so all three failure shapes -- a JSON object with no `ok`, a JSON object whose `ok` is a string, and a body that is not JSON at all -- produced `ok == true`. `report()` at main.swift:139 then printed "ok" or "refused" and returned, and the three arms that use it (`workspace create`, `workspace delete`, `session archive`) fell out of the switch and exited 0; `prompt` (:286) and `prompt-all` (:297) had already been given `exit(outcome.ok ? 0 : 1)` for the same information, so the tool answered one event with two statuses. Measured live against the release binary at 0038abf with a stub member on 127.0.0.1:39807 that answers the group read normally and then answers `POST /dsh-lan/workspaces` in five shapes, exit code read straight from the process (no pipe): `{"ok":true,...}` -> stdout `ok`, exit 0; `{"workspaceId":"ws-new"}` -> stdout `ok`, exit 0; `{"ok":"true"}` -> stdout `ok`, exit 0; `{"ok":false,"message":"disk full"}` -> stdout `refused`, exit 0; a 200 `text/html` proxy page -> stdout `ok`, exit 0. Reach, stated honestly: the plugin's own router answers every 2xx with `ok: true` and refuses with an ApiError status -- measured: 14 `ok: true` reply bodies in router.js, all 10 single-line `return { body:` sites carrying it, and a grep for a 2xx reply without it finds none -- and `git log -S "ok: true" -- router.js`'s oldest entry is the router's first commit `0ddce77`, so no version of our server ever produced these shapes. The defect is reachable from what is *not* our server: a transparent proxy or captive portal on the LAN, a port squat, or a member running something else. `workspace delete --workspace ID` archives sessions as it goes, so the arm that misreads most confidently is also the destructive one.

**Fix.** Two halves. `ack()` now requires the 2xx body to be a JSON object carrying a boolean `ok`, and throws the error that already existed for exactly this shape -- `FleetError.decoding(target:reason: "a 2xx answer carries no boolean `ok`")` -- instead of assuming it; a thrown error reaches `fail()` and exits 1, the same path a 401 already took. `report()` now exits `ack.ok ? 0 : 1`, so all five action arms answer a refusal with the same status, and the usage text says the contract out loud ("An action exits 0 only when the Mac that owns it confirms it") because a status a script branches on is a contract, and until now nothing documented it. No other call site changed: `prompt`/`prompt-all` already exited on `.ok`, and the dashboard's `FleetRenderer` label for a refusal (FleetCommands.swift:371) reads `ack.ok` and was already correct. `FleetAck.raw` still carries the verbatim body for `--json`.

**Evidence after.** TDD, in that order. The three tests went in first and failed for the right reason -- `swift test --no-parallel --filter FleetRoutingTests` exit 1, three issues, each "an error was expected but none was thrown" at FleetTests.swift:248/265/284 -- pinning `anAckThatCarriesNoBooleanOkIsNotAnAck`, `anAckWhoseOkIsAStringIsNotAnAck` and `aTwoHundredPageThatIsNotJSONIsNotAnAck` (FleetTests.swift:238/258/274) against the exact `FleetError.decoding` value including the target and the message an operator sees. After the fix the same filter is exit 0, 9 tests in 1 suite, and the whole suite is exit 0 at 1698 tests in 252 suites -- 1695 plus these three. The guard covers all four `ack()` call sites (prompt, createWorkspace, deleteWorkspace, archive) because the check sits in the shared decode, not in each method. Re-measured live on the rebuilt release binary with the same stub, one fresh ephemeral loopback port per arm, and the same unmasked exit codes: `{"ok":true}` -> stdout `ok`, exit 0; no-`ok` -> exit 1 with "<peer> answered something unreadable: a 2xx answer carries no boolean `ok`"; string `ok` -> exit 1, same; `{"ok":false}` -> stdout `refused`, exit 1; 200 HTML -> exit 1, same message. So the honest arm still succeeds and the four dishonest arms now fail loudly. Sibling sweep of the same pattern -- every `?? true` in `sources/` (10 sites) -- found one other fail-open-looking site and it was tested and withdrawn: `Sampler.lastRowHadFiniteLogit`'s `.tiled` arm reads `softcapTiled?.rowMax.isFinite ?? true`, but `softcapTiled` is assigned unconditionally in `init` (Sampler.swift:59) and `lastFrontEnd = .tiled` is only set inside `if samplerPath == .tiled, let softcapTiled` (:110), so the nil arm is unreachable and the default cannot mask a NaN row. The server's `?? true` on content-type (HTTPServerHandler+Routes.swift:54) is the deliberate AUD-132/147 absent-header contract, documented at the line. The rest are spec defaults (`store ?? true`, `parallelToolCalls ?? true`), HF config defaults (`norm_topk_prob`, `tie_word_embeddings`), or idioms (`isEmpty ?? true`, first-candidate `?? true`). THE LIMITATION: the exit-status half is not unit-testable from this tree -- `report()` lives in the executable's top-level code and no fleet test spawns the binary -- so it is pinned by the live probe above, which is reproducible but not a gate; the fail-open half is pinned by tests that fail observably. `./tools/lint.sh all` over this tree: 17 of 18 gates ok, and the eighteenth fails on the host rather than the change -- brew had installed ruff 0.16.10 into /opt/homebrew/bin, which shadows pipx's pinned 0.16.7 at ~/.local/bin; with the pinned binary first on PATH the same gate reports ok (check and format clean, parses under 3.13). The gate is right to fail: a drifted linter is an untested linter.

### AUD-184 — A bound that means the opposite of what was asked: `--limit 0` prompts every session in the group, `--timeout 0` never times out at all, and `--width 0` prints the "terminal too small" message as nothing

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier B
- **Project:** fleet
- **Location:** `sources/TinyTitanFleet/Core/FleetCommands.swift:188-189 (the `if let limit, limit > 0` guard that reads a cap as "no cap"), sources/TinyTitanFleet/Command/main.swift:81,87-88,92-93 (`--timeout`, `--limit`, `--concurrency`, `--width`, `--height` read by `numberOption` with no range), sources/TinyTitanFleet/Core/FleetDashboardView.swift:39 (`tooSmall` fitting its own remedy to the width it is complaining about)`
- **Category:** integrity / fail-silent range handling: a numeric value that cannot mean what the flag is for is obeyed in the opposite direction
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** The limit AUD-183 named and deliberately left unfixed ("out-of-range numbers are still accepted"), measured to the end rather than assumed: three probes -- a stub member holding four live sessions, a stub that accepts a connection and never answers, and the release binary at each size around its own documented minimum.

**Evidence before.** All three parts measured against the shipped release binary at `1b4041e` with exit codes read straight from the process. (1) `prompt-all --limit`: against a stub member on 127.0.0.1:39871 exposing four active sessions and recording every prompt it receives (`/tmp/probe184.out`), `--limit 1` reports `considered: 1, delivered: 1` and the stub records 1 prompt, `--limit 4` records 4 -- and `--limit 0`, `--limit -1` and no `--limit` at all each report `considered: 4, delivered: 4` with `ok: true`, exit 0, stub records 4. A cap of zero is therefore read as "no cap": asking to bound the broadcast to nothing prompts every session on every Mac in the group. `FleetCommands.swift:188` is the line, `if let limit, limit > 0`, and it is the only thing between that call and `Array.prefix(_:)`, which traps -- measured with `swift` on this toolchain: `Array(1...4).prefix(-1)` is `Fatal error: Can't take a prefix of negative length from a collection`, exit 133. So the guard that prevents a crash is also what inverts the meaning, and a library caller that drops it inherits the trap. `--concurrency -3` on the same stub delivers to all 4 with exit 0, because the batch is clamped by `max(1, concurrency)` and the operator is never told the number they typed was thrown away. (2) `--timeout`: `URLSessionConfiguration.timeoutIntervalForRequest` treats a non-positive value as no timeout. Against a stub that accepts and never answers (127.0.0.1:39899, `/tmp/probe_timeout.out`), `--timeout 2` reports `is unreachable: The request timed out.` in 3 s and exit 1, while `--timeout 0` and `--timeout -5` were still hanging when a 14 s watchdog killed them (exit 137, no output). The control-plane CLI therefore has a documented flag that can turn any read into an unbounded wait, and the operator's only answer is Ctrl-C. (3) `--width`/`--height`: `FleetDashboardView.render` guards with `width >= minimumWidth, height >= minimumHeight` and returns `tooSmall`, which builds `[fit("", width), fit(center(message, width), width)]`, and `fit` returns "" for `width <= 0` (FleetDashboardView.swift:327). Measured at each size (`/tmp/probe_size.out`): `--width 44` prints a normal 30-line frame, `--width 43` prints `terminal too small — need 44×6, have 43×30`, `--width 10` prints `terminal …`, `--width 1` prints `…`, and `--width 0` and `--width -5` print **0 bytes**; `--height 1`, `--height 0` and `--height -5` each print one line of padding, because `prefix(max(1, height))` keeps the blank line and drops the message. Every one of those exits 0. The remedy the guard exists to give the operator is destroyed by the very size it reports. Reach: `ttlanmanager` has no in-tree caller (`grep -rn ttlanmanager plugins tools benchmark` is three comments, no call), so no automation here changes shape; `top`'s interactive path is not affected by (3) because `FleetTerminal.Size` already falls back to 100x30 when the ioctl reports zero columns, which is why the CLI flags -- they bypass that fallback -- are the route. The server-side sibling is real and is filed separately, not fixed here: `promptAllActive` in plugins/dsh-lan-manager/src/api.js:767-768 caps with `Number.isInteger(options.limit) && options.limit > 0 ? wanted.slice(0, options.limit) : wanted`, so `POST /dsh-lan/prompt-all {"prompt":...,"limit":0}` prompts every active session on that Mac, the same inversion one layer down and reachable by any client of the loopback route. Its positive branch is pinned (router.test.js:549, "prompt-all can be narrowed to specific sessions and capped", asserts `limit: 2` delivers 2), and its non-positive branch is not tested at all -- no test in the package sends `limit: 0` or a negative -- so the escalation is exactly the uncovered half. The two other `limit` readers in the plugin were checked and are not this defect: `messageLimit` (api.js:585-589) sends a non-positive or unparseable `?limit=` to the documented default rather than to everything, and `mapLimit` (peers.js:183) clamps with `Math.max(1, ...)` before it opens runners.

**Fix.** Three halves, one rule: a bound is honoured in the direction the flag means, or the run refuses. `positiveOption` (main.swift) now reads `--timeout`, `--limit`, `--concurrency`, `--width` and `--height`, and fails with `X needs a positive number, not Y` naming the flag and the value before any request goes out; it is generic over `LosslessStringConvertible & Comparable & ExpressibleByIntegerLiteral` so the Double timeout and the four Int counts share one message and one check. `--interval` deliberately still goes through `numberOption`: its floor is documented behaviour ("default 30 s, floored at 2 s") and `FleetScanner` clamps it, so `--interval 1` meaning 2 s is the contract, not a wrong answer. `promptAll`'s cap is now literal -- `if let limit { work = Array(work.prefix(max(0, limit))) }` -- so a library caller asking for zero sessions gets none and a negative one cannot reach the trap; `max(1, concurrency)` stays, and it is load-bearing: measured on this toolchain, `stride(from: 0, to: 4, by: 0)` is `Fatal error: Stride size must not be zero` and exit 133, so a zero batch size is a crash the CLI would otherwise hand to the library. `tooSmall` prints its message when the window cannot hold it (`width >= message.count ? fit(center(...)) : message`) and puts the message first when there is only one line, so the guard's remedy survives the size that triggered it; that is the one place this tree prints past the width it was handed, and the comment says so and why. `--help` now states the rule. No default moved: timeout is still 10 s, concurrency still 4, `top` still 100x30 with a 30 s scan.

**Evidence after.** TDD, in that order. Five tests went in first and failed for the right reason (`/tmp/red184.log`, `/tmp/red184b.log`): `aLimitOfZeroPromptsNoSessionsRatherThanAllOfThem` and `aNegativeLimitPromptsNoSessionsAndDoesNotTrap` failed on `outcomes.isEmpty` and on the transport recording two calls where zero were asked for (FleetTests.swift:203-204, 218-219); `theTooSmallMessageSurvivesASizeThatCannotHoldIt` failed at all six sizes (DashboardTests.swift:99); `aNumberThatCannotMeanWhatTheFlagSaysIsRefused` failed the stderr-content assertions for each of the five flags. Two things about those runs are worth recording rather than glossing: the first version of the library tests did not compile, because `await` inside a `#expect` message autoclosure is not allowed, which is a build failure and not a RED, so it was fixed and the real failure observed after it; and the CLI test's `status != 0` assertion passed *before* the fix for the wrong reason -- the peer those arms dial is 127.0.0.1:1, which refuses, so the run already exited 1. What actually pins the behaviour is the pair of message assertions, and after the timeout arms were added the observed RED was exactly the two new arms (5 issues) while the five already-fixed flags passed -- the assertion set discriminates. After the fix: `--filter FleetUsageTests --filter FleetRoutingTests --filter FleetDashboardLayoutTests` exits 0 at 23 tests in 3 suites, `swift build -c release` exits 0 with no warning, and the release re-probe is measured (`/tmp/probe184after.out`): `--limit 1` -> considered 1, stub saw 1; `--limit 2` -> 2 and 2; `--limit 0` and `--limit -1` -> exit 1 `--limit needs a positive number, not 0`, stub saw **0** prompts; `--concurrency 0` -> exit 1, stub saw 0; no `--limit` -> 4 as documented. `--timeout 0` and `--timeout -5` against the silent stub now exit 1 in 0 s with the message, against 14 s-and-still-hanging before. `--width 0`/`--width -5`/`--height 0`/`--height -5` -> exit 1 refused; `--width 1` prints `terminal too small — need 44×6, have 1×30` and `--height 1` prints the same message instead of a line of padding; `--width 44` still prints a normal frame. `--filter FleetUsageTests/helpNamesEveryOptionTheParserReads` still holds over the re-wrapped help (21 options, `[]` undocumented, `[]` phantom). The whole serial suite and all eighteen gates were then run on this tree: `swift test --no-parallel` exits 0 at 1705 tests in 253 suites across the seven test bundles with no `recorded an issue` line anywhere in the log (`/tmp/suite184.log`), and `PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" ./tools/lint.sh all` exits 0 over all eighteen gates, the python one reading the pinned `ruff 0.16.7` rather than the Homebrew 0.16.10 this host puts on `PATH` (`/tmp/lint184.log`). What is *not* covered: the plugin's `POST /prompt-all {"limit":0}` inversion is unfixed and deliberately out of this row's reach, since it changes a wire contract and has no test fixture yet -- filed as its own row. And the range rule lives in the CLI plus the one library call that inverted it: `--limit 7` on a group of four is still accepted and simply delivers four, which is what a cap means.

### AUD-185 — The route's copy of the same inversion: `{"limit":0}` prompts every session on that Mac, `{"sessionIds":[]}` and `{"sessionIds":"s-a1"}` do too, and `{"limit":"2"}` is a cap silently thrown away

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier B
- **Project:** plugins
- **Location:** `plugins/dsh-lan-manager/src/api.js:760-767 (`promptAllActive`, the two guards that read an unreadable bound as "everyone"), plugins/dsh-lan-manager/src/router.js:601-609 (`POST /prompt-all` hands the whole body to it)`
- **Category:** integrity / fail-silent range handling: a wire value that cannot be read as a bound is obeyed in the opposite direction
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** The sibling AUD-184 named and deliberately left unfixed rather than bundling a wire-contract change into a CLI row. Read at the source first, then measured: `promptAllActive` guarded its filter with `Array.isArray(options.sessionIds) && options.sessionIds.length > 0` and its cap with `Number.isInteger(options.limit) && options.limit > 0`, each falling through to "everyone" when the test failed -- the same shape as `FleetCommands.swift:188`. Its positive branch is pinned by `test/router.test.js:549` (`limit: 2` delivers 2); its non-positive ones were tested by nothing.

**Evidence before.** Measured through the real router with the harness's own fake agents, three active sessions (`s-a1`, `s-a2`, `s-b1`), against the tree at `84f2207` staged into `/tmp/pre185` so the pre-fix code is what ran. One probe, eight bodies (`/tmp/probe185.log`), each printing the status, the delivered count and the session ids that actually received the prompt: `{"limit":0}` -> 200, 3 delivered, s-a1,s-a2,s-b1; `{"limit":-1}` -> 200, 3 delivered; `{"limit":1.5}` -> 200, 3 delivered; `{"limit":"2"}` -> 200, 3 delivered; `{"limit":null}` -> 200, 3 delivered; `{"sessionIds":[]}` -> 200, 3 delivered; `{"sessionIds":"s-a1"}` -> 200, 3 delivered -- a request naming exactly one session prompts the whole fleet, which is the worst of the set; and `{"sessionIds":["s-a1"],"limit":0}` -> 200, 1 delivered, so a cap of zero is not merely ignored, it is ignored while looking like it worked. Every one answers `ok: true`. Reach: the documented route (`README.md:317-323` lists both keys as optional, with no bound stated) and `promptAllActive`, exported from `src/index.js:72`. No in-tree client sends either key -- `grep -rn prompt-all` finds only the router, the README's two examples (neither sets a bound) and the tests, and `ttlanmanager` does its fan-out client-side over `POST /prompt` per session (`sources/TinyTitanFleet/Core/FleetCommands.swift` never dials `/prompt-all`) -- so this is a wire contract for an outside caller, not a broken sibling of a working CLI. What is NOT verified: no live DeepSeek Harness instance was driven, because a model run is a separate operator-requested job and the routes here are exercised end to end through the real router in the suite; the fake ctx is the harness's own shape.

**Fix.** One rule, the AUD-184 rule, on the wire side: a bound is honoured in the direction it means, or the request is refused. `promptAllActive` now rejects a present-but-unreadable value with `ApiError(Failure.BAD_REQUEST, …, 400)` before anything is delivered -- `sessionIds` must be an array if it is there at all, `limit` must be a positive integer -- and an absent key still means everyone, which is what the route is for. The two then read literally: `sessionIds: []` filters to nothing, and a valid `limit` slices. The validation lives in `api.js` rather than the route because that is where this module already validates its own inputs and answers 400 (`toContent`, api.js:198-210, refuses an empty prompt the same way), so the exported helper cannot be called into the inversion by a non-HTTP caller either. `README.md:320` now states the bound instead of leaving "optional" to mean "any value". Siblings swept and cleared, with the reason: `messageLimit` (api.js:585-589) turns a non-positive `?limit=` into `DEFAULT_MESSAGE_LIMIT` and clamps to `MAX_MESSAGE_LIMIT`, so it can never mean "the whole history"; `mapLimit` (peers.js:183) is clamped; `positive`/`probeTimeout` (config.js:240,253) are a documented explicit-then-env-then-default chain that lands on bounded defaults, not on "unbounded"; `tailscalePeers` (discovery.js:173) returns `[]` on an empty parse, never "all peers"; and the Swift caller was fixed in AUD-184. The guard that stops recurrence is the three route tests plus the README line.

**Evidence after.** TDD, in that order. Three tests went into `plugins/dsh-lan-manager/test/router.test.js` first and all three failed for the right reason (`/tmp/red185.log`, exit 1, 138 pass / 3 fail): `prompt-all refuses a limit that cannot mean a cap` failed on `limit 0 was accepted / 200 !== 400`; `prompt-all refuses a target list it cannot read` failed with the whole response body in the message, showing 3 sessions delivered to a request that named one; `prompt-all delivers an empty session list to nothing, not to everyone` failed on `an empty target list prompted the fleet / 3 !== 0`. After the fix the same file runs 70 tests (67 before it, plus these three) with no failure, and the package suite is 141 tests, 141 pass, 0 fail, exit 0. Re-measured through the same eight-body probe against the fixed tree (`/tmp/probe185-after.log`): each of `limit` 0, -1, 1.5, "2", null -> 400 with nothing delivered; `sessionIds: "s-a1"` -> 400; `{"sessionIds":["s-a1"],"limit":0}` -> 400 instead of a silently ignored cap; and `{"sessionIds":[]}` -> 200 with `delivered: []`, `total: 0`, i.e. the fail-safe answer to an empty target list is nothing, never everything. The two positive controls are the pre-existing tests, which were not touched and still pass: `prompt-all fans out across every visible session` (no keys -> 3) and `prompt-all can be narrowed to specific sessions and capped` (`limit: 2` -> 2, `sessionIds: ["s-b1"]` -> 1). `npm test` in `plugins/dsh-tinytitan` exit 0 (its own suite, untouched by this row but run because both packages share the gate), `tools/lint.sh javascript` (pinned eslint 10.11.0 / prettier 3.9.9) ok for both packages, `swift test --no-parallel` exit 0 at 1705 tests in 253 suites with zero issue lines, and `PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" ./tools/lint.sh all` -- all eighteen gates on the pinned tools -- exit 0 over the same tree.
