(a) ane_steady_state_decode's prefill line sat behind `if prefill['gpu'] and prefill['ane']`, so handing it rows whose ANE `prefill_s` is 0.0 printed no prefill line at all -- neither arm's median -- and the page still read `sweep status 0`, because `metric_count` had already counted that zero as measured and so raised no note. (b) the same shape at its window loop (`if gpu[0] and ane[0]`) deleted a window's comparison line for a 0.0 tok/s median: on the GPU side the divisor, with no reason printed, and on the ANE side a real result -- that arm 100 percent slower over that window -- dropped rather than published. (c) tinytitan_mtp_b3_qualification's guard was `None in (off_rate, on_rate, accept, emitted, delta) or not off_rate`, and `delta` is None exactly when `off_rate` is zero, so a control arm that logged `tok/s=0.00` refused as `an arm carried no rate` -- a cause that did not happen -- and printed neither arm's median. (d) the same driver's runs listing read `r['decode_tok_s']`, so an arm whose median was measured over part of its rows -- the exact shape `metric_count` exists to report as `over 1 of 2` -- raised `KeyError: 'decode_tok_s'` out of the print line after the header had already gone to stdout. (e) ane_prefill_ab_matrix's `if off and on and ...` left no `speedup` key for an ANE median of 0.0 s and its note chain had nothing to say, so the published row printed both medians beside a bare `-`; and `if tokens and tokens < chunk` skipped the under-one-chunk note for a prompt that logged `0tok` while still publishing a `speedup` for a prompt the ANE cannot serve.

**Fix.** absence and zero are now two different answers, and the difference is which side of the divide the figure sits on. A zero divisor refuses with the zero named and its own status -- `NOT MEASURED: the ANE arm's prefill median is 0 s, so the speedup would divide by zero`, `the GPU arm's 64-token window is 0 tok/s`, `the off arm's median is 0 tok/s, so no delta is computable` -- the last being the wording tinytitan_mtp_phases.py:267 already used, so the three siblings now agree instead of one of them inventing the rule. A zero numerator is published as the figure it is: a 0.00 s GPU prefill gives `speedup 0.00x`, a 0-token prompt gets the chunk note the guard exists to give, and a 0.0 percent acceptance prints and refuses on its own out-of-domain grounds. A refusal no longer hides the cells it is about: the steady-state prefill line prints through the shared `logged()`, and the B3 medians and acceptance line print whenever they are measured. The runs listing reads with `r.get(...)` like its sibling at tinytitan_ane_prefill_ab.py:216, so a partial arm shows `[8.0, None]` beside the `over 1 of 2` that already counts it. No new status vocabulary: every refusal reuses the NOT MEASURED token the driver's own status function already turns into a 2.

**Commit.** `e1fddc1`

**Evidence before.** a probe table against HEAD, model-free: hit('crimson', '') was True, hit('crimson', '   ') was True, hit('crimson-blue', 'crimson') was True and hit('', 'Postgres 16') was True, because the last line of the scorer tested both directions of containment. memory_master.py:261 feeds exactly this function with result['answers'].get(key) and sums the result into the per-session recall score, and :271 uses it to decide whether an answer changed, so a session whose quiz field was present but blank counted as a retrieval and a blank-then-blank pair counted as unchanged. **Evidence after.** five tests added to MatchingTests in the owner suite benchmark/test_memory_master.py: three RED at HEAD (a blank answer, a truncated answer, an empty expected value) and two controls that already held (an absent answer reaching the None guard, and the collision needles for it). The guard's first test was wrong and is recorded rather than hidden: it used hit('none', None), which cannot collide because str(None) is capitalised, so the mutant survived until the test was rewritten as hit('on', None) and hit('ne', None). ### AUD-288 — the recall scorer read silence as a NO, so a dead engine was scored as a wrong one and an empty answer file printed recall@1 0/0 at exit 0

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** benchmark
- **Location:** `benchmark/side_engine_recall.py:171-277 (post-fix), benchmark/side_engine_recall.py:8, 100-131`
- **Category:** a blank judgement read as NO: the side-engine recall scorer scored a dead or silent engine as a wrong one, ranked every unjudged fact last by construction, and divided its rates by however many questions survived, so an empty answer file printed a measured 0/0 and exited 0
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** the three drivers AUD-286's sweep left unread, this one measured second. Model-free throughout: the driver is a python ranker over an authored book, so every shape was produced by writing a fixture jsonl and calling score() -- no model, no server binary, nothing fetched.

**Evidence before.** six shapes measured against HEAD. (1) `--score` on an empty file printed `token ranking: recall@1 0/0  recall@3 0/0` and `side-engine: recall@1 0/0  recall@3 0/0` and returned 0 -- AUD-233's denominator-is-its-survivors shape, here in the comparison the memory matrix publishes. (2) the same command on a path that does not exist escaped as a traceback and answered 1, the status a contested figure carries. (3) every judgement was `(row.get('completion') or '').strip().upper().startswith('YES')`, so a row whose completion was blank or absent was counted as an answered NO: an engine that never ran, or one that errored, was scored as an engine that disagreed. (4) `t7_rank` is built over the entire `BIBLE`, so a fact with no judged row was ranked last by construction rather than left unranked -- a group that judged 3 of 10 facts was scored as if it had judged all 10 and got 3 wrong. (5) the rates divided by however many questions produced rows, so a run in which 1 of 4 fair questions ran printed a headline over 1. (6) the module docstring stated the value term scores 1 while the code and `docs/side-engine-tasks.md:290` both say 2, a fossil of the scorer before `878cea6`.

**Fix.** `--score` answers a status now, printed in the module docstring: 0 every fair question ran, answered every fact and every answer was there; 1 a named fair question ran no rows, left facts unanswered, or carried rows with no judgement, so the rates cover part of the matrix; 2 the comparison does not exist -- reason printed, no rates printed. A `judgement()` helper returns `None` for a blank or absent completion, so silence is excluded from the denominators instead of read as NO, and an `exclusions()` helper names why a question left the score. Reading, validation and the missing-file case all route through one `refuse()`. The shipped reading is preserved and pinned: `strip().upper()` and `startswith('YES')` still accept lower-case answers, leading whitespace and a rambling NO, because that leniency is what the recorded runs were produced with. The docstring's value weight is corrected 1 to 2 as prose, not numerics, and `deterministic_rank` now names the two terms the Swift scorer adds and this mirror does not model: tags, and `record.importance` raised on top of the text score.

**Evidence after.** 17 tests in the new owner suite `benchmark/test_side_engine_recall_verdict.py`, `git add`ed before CI named it (AUD-211): 15 RED at HEAD, 2 controls written to pin the preserved leniency (a lower-case and whitespace-padded answer, and a rambling NO whose expected ranking is computed from `driver.BIBLE` rather than asserted). Sweep: 25 single-hit anchored mutants over the pristine copy, 0 survivors, source restored byte-identical by md5; the two survivors that appeared mid-sweep became tests rather than deleted mutants. Suite OK. The CI verdict group is 49 suites and 1070 tests OK on python3.13. CLI statuses measured end to end on fixtures: a full honest run answers 0, a run with one question missing answers 1, a run with silent rows answers 1, an empty file answers 2 and prints no rates. `--baseline` unchanged on the figures it publishes: `mechanical 10/10`, `paraphrased recall@1 3/4 recall@3 3/4`, `1 of 4 missed at rank 1`. `bash tools/lint.sh all` rc=0; ruff 0.16.7 clean and formatted. Fix commit 498795a.

### AUD-291 — a judge that wrote no rows answers 0, `measured nothing: every request refused` prints over a file with no requests, and 2 rows of a 60-case run pass

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** benchmark
- **Location:** `benchmark/side_engine_judges.py:27-34 (status table), :117-120 (refuse), :123-145 (read_rows), :148-174 (tally/summarize), :199-207 (line), :224-285 (main verdict), benchmark/test_side_engine_judges.py:87 (guard placement)`
- **Category:** a verdict that is the negation of a coverage check: the judges driver answers 0 for a done file that holds no rows, prints a refusal message over a run that refused nothing, and never compares the rows it scored against the jobs it was given
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-289's sibling sweep: the last driver in the side-engine `--score` family, read for the hole AUD-288 and AUD-289 closed. Measured against HEAD at 1ba59a1, model-free -- `summarize()` and `line()` were called on fixture done files, so no model, no server, nothing fetched.

**Evidence before.** five shapes measured. (1) `summarize()` over a done file with no rows returns `{}`, and the verdict is `1 if any(entry['refused'] for entry in per_task.values()) else 0`, which is False over an empty map: a judge whose done file holds nothing answers 0. (2) The same run prints, from `line()`, `measured nothing: every request refused, so none of the above is a score` -- the wording names refusals when zero requests ran, so the message and the status disagree about what happened. (3) Coverage: over the authored 60 cases, a done file holding 2 answered rows gives `{'T2': {'correct': 2, 'total': 2, 'refused': 0}}` and answers 0; `len(jobs)` is passed to `line()` for the s/judgement rate and never reaches the verdict, so a run that died after 2 of 60 judgements is a clean pass. (4) `summarize(<missing path>)` raises `FileNotFoundError`, a half-written line raises `JSONDecodeError`, a row with no `task` raises `KeyError`, and a row with a `task` but no `prompt` raises `KeyError` out of `side_engine_tasks.truth_of:167`; `main()` reads `args.jobs` unguarded too. **Fix.** `refuse()` names the reason, prints no table and answers 2. `read_rows()` returns (rows, reason) and owns every unreadable shape -- a path that cannot be read, a line that is not json, a row that names no task/prompt/truth, a file with no rows -- and `main()` refuses on each instead of reaching the table. `tally()` counts a row that carried neither a completion nor an error as `silent`, out of every denominator, where before a blank completion entered the count as a judgement and, for a file of nothing but blanks, was the only thing the verdict could see. `line()` prints `measured nothing: every request refused` only where requests refused and the silent count only where rows went unanswered, and prints a rate only over judgements that exist. `main()` now prints `judged N of M jobs, R refused, S with no answer`, names the shortfall or the surplus whenever `len(rows) != len(jobs)`, and returns 1 when `judged != len(jobs)`; the jobs file itself is read under the same guards. The reading of an answer is untouched -- `truth_of`, `strip().upper()`, the first word and the `.,:;\"'` strip -- so the recorded `4B 7/8`, `9B 8/8` and `recall@1 3/4` figures still mean what they meant.

**Evidence after.** measured: the new suite answers 15 of its 17 tests RED at HEAD before the driver changed (8 failures, 5 errors), the 2 that pass at HEAD are labelled in their docstrings as preservation pins, not guards. ### AUD-292 — `zero false positives` at exit 0 with the stub rule printing `no corpus`; a measured trip answers 2 and an absent corpus answers 1, where the tree reads 2 as NOT MEASURED

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** benchmark
- **Location:** `benchmark/watchdog_calibrate.py:345-350 (clean), :301-308 (the no-corpus stub row), :261-264 (no replies), :322-324 (pingpong outside the verdict), :353-368 (selftest)`
- **Category:** a calibration that answered 0 over a corpus one of its two rules never saw; its status codes stay the tree's outlier, now a row of their own
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-291's sibling sweep: the last driver AUD-286's sweep left unread, read for the absence and coverage seams. Measured against HEAD at 1b25ef2, model-free -- `main()` and `selftest()` were called with `replies`, `exchanges` and `tool_conversations` patched to in-memory fixture corpora, so no log tree was opened and nothing fetched.

**Evidence before.** four shapes measured. (1) A reply corpus of one non-tripping reply with `exchanges()` patched to nothing: the stub row prints `no corpus`, and the run prints `zero false positives on 1 replies` and answers 0 -- the same 0 the identical corpus with one recorded exchange answers, so a full calibration and one that never applied the stub rule are indistinguishable by status. (2) `tool_conversations()` is not in `clean` at all: the pingpong watchdog prints `no corpus` in both runs above and neither a trip there nor an absent corpus could ever contest the 0. (3) The codes run the other way: a measured trip answers 2, which every driver AUD-273 through AUD-291 reserves for NOT MEASURED, and `main()` with no replies answers 1 with `no recorded replies under <path>` printed -- a run that measured nothing wearing the status of a contested measurement. (4) `selftest()` with a missing fixture answers the same 1 for the same reason. For contrast, what the driver does hold: a reply that trips the loop detector is counted and named, and the exchange shortfall is printed honestly in its own row -- the defect is that the printout is honest and the status is not.

**Fix.** `clean` reads `not loop_hits and not stub_hits and not pingpong`, so a tool-call conversation that trips the ping-pong watchdog is a false positive that contests the run. The codes themselves were pinned rather than renumbered onto the 0 / 1 contested / 2 NOT MEASURED table the other drivers answer, because that is AUD-293's decision to make.

**Evidence after.** measured: `benchmark/test_watchdog_calibrate_verdict.py` (11 tests, `git add`ed before CI named it, AUD-211) run against `git show 5ddc1a8^:benchmark/watchdog_calibrate.py` gives 4 RED -- test_no_recorded_exchanges_cannot_certify_the_stub_rule, test_no_recorded_conversations_cannot_certify_the_pingpong_rule, test_a_pingpong_trip_is_a_false_positive_and_not_a_clean_run and test_a_measured_trip_outranks_a_rule_that_saw_nothing -- and 7 pass there, 2 of them labelled preservation pins in their docstrings (the clean run answers 0, a measured trip answers 2) and 5 holding behaviour the driver already had (`selftest()`'s three verdicts, the no-replies refusal, the stall row's `not applicable`). ### AUD-294 — `tools/ane_sidecars.sh` gates an install and answers 0 with `verified: 0` when the models directory is empty, missing, or holds no manifest -- four shapes measured, all 0

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** tools
- **Location:** `benchmark-side note in `tools/ane_sidecars.sh:76-83` (candidate collection), :85-87 (the loop that does not run), :160-168 (the counts and `exit 0`)`
- **Category:** a gate that reports a pass over a directory it found nothing in: zero candidates is the same exit as every install verified
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** the sweep after AUD-292's close, taken over the harnesses no suite or CI step names (`grep` of every `tools/*.sh` and `benchmark/*.sh` against the text of every suite and the workflow): two files came back unnamed, `benchmark/combos.sh` and `tools/ane_sidecars.sh`. The first is a three-line `exec` forwarder whose status passes through, so it has no verdict of its own. The second is the sidecar gate `docs/adding-a-model.md:128` tells an operator to run, and its own header says it `exits non-zero if any model it was asked about is still without a verified sidecar, so it can gate an install`. AUD-253's sibling sweep already read this file and cleared it for the AND-OR status seam (`exit 1` before the final `exit 0`); the question that sweep did not ask is what the script does when the loop has nothing to iterate.

**Evidence before.** four shapes, all measured by running the real script with `TINYTITAN_MODELS_DIR` pointed at a temp tree and `TINYTITAN_COREML_PYTHON` set to `/usr/bin/false` so nothing could export, verify or be reached -- no model, no install touched, nothing fetched. (a) An existing but empty models directory: prints `verified: 0`, exit **0**. (b) A directory holding `other-dir/` with no `manifest.json`: prints `verified: 0`, exit **0** -- the glob finds a subdirectory, the manifest test rejects it, and the candidate list ends up empty by a different route. (c) A models directory that does not exist at all: prints `verified: 0`, exit **0**, and names nothing -- the failed glob is silent, so the reader cannot tell an absent directory from an installed family the script chose to skip. (d) `--verify-only` over (a): the same, exit **0**, which is the mode a check would run against installs it believes are there. For contrast, what the script does hold, and it holds it well: a *named* install that is not there prints `no manifest at <path> -- not installed` and exits 1 (measured); an unknown option exits 2; a `--chunk` the runtime would not route is refused before any work; the export is deliberately not piped so a `tail` cannot borrow its status (:122-126 carries the comment saying so); and a verification failure lands in `failed`. The defect is the empty case only, and it is the class this audit has closed repeatedly: AUD-210 over a record that compared zero metrics, AUD-233's `Answers verified: 0/0` reported as COMPLETE, AUD-240's reports certifying clean over a directory that holds no run, and `tools/lint.sh`'s own `unbounded-read` and `test-hollow` gates, which fail rather than report ok when their walk found no files. The sibling harness already has the guard this one lacks: `tools/install_models.sh:794-797` refuses an empty catalogue with the reason on stderr and `return 2`.

**Fix.** `tools/ane_sidecars.sh:90-103` refuses the empty walk: zero candidates after collection names `$MODELS_DIR`, says what a candidate is and that a fresh clone has no `models/` at all, states that nothing was exported and nothing was verified, and exits 2 -- the code the script already answers for a usage refusal, so its table stays three statuses: 0 every candidate the walk found is verified, 1 one it was asked about is not, 2 it did not get to run. The header (:22-28) now spells that table out and `usage()` was moved from `sed -n '2,24p'` to `'2,28p'`: the header grew by five lines, and a line-range usage prints the first code line when its range falls short -- `set -euo pipefail` was the next line. A directory whose installs are all skipped families keeps exit 0 with `verified: 0` and the reason, because those were asked about. Found while testing it and fixed in the same commit: the family read at :114-124 was a bare command substitution, so an interpreter that could not read a manifest ended the whole run under `set -e` with status 1 and no word about which install or which file; it now prints `!! <name>: <interpreter> could not read the family from <path>` and lands in `failed`.

**Evidence after.** Written first, and it failed first: the last RED run measures 7 of 15 tests failing against the unpatched driver -- the four empty-walk shapes each returned 0 where 2 was asked for, the refusal text was absent, the silent family read printed nothing, and the usage pin caught the header growing past its `sed` range. Two earlier RED runs showed 11 of 14 and 8 of 14, and those failures were mine rather than the script's: a fixture family spelled `qwen_3_5_dense` where the driver's case is `qwen3_5_dense`, and an assertion that the verification-failure message lands on stdout where the script correctly writes stderr. Both were reported as the test being wrong before the test was touched. GREEN took three runs -- the first two each left exactly the usage pin failing, because the header grew to five lines while the range edit lagged it -- then 15 OK, then the class that pins the range from both sides was added and 16 tests OK. The four shapes now measure: empty `models/` exit **2** naming the directory, `other-dir/` with no manifest exit **2**, an absent `models/` exit **2**, `--verify-only` over the empty one exit **2**, and the refusal text lands on stderr so it cannot be read as a report line. Eight verdicts that were already right are pinned so the guard cannot be paid for with a regression: a named install that is not there 1, an unknown option 2, an unroutable `--chunk` 2, export+verify 0 with `verified: 1`, a non-default chunk verified against `ane_prefill-1024`, a skipped family 0 with the reason, a verification failure 1 with the message on stderr, a failed export 1 naming the model and leaving no sidecar directory behind. Nineteen single-hit anchored mutants of the driver, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`: the first sweep left one survivor, `manifest: the unreadable one is counted but never named`, which stayed green because the assertion meant to catch it matched a phrase the `FAILED :` summary line also prints -- the AUD-292 lesson again, an `assertIn` satisfied by a different line than the one that names the cause. Strengthened to assert the per-model line, and re-run against the committed driver: 19 mutants, **0 survivors**, 0 bad anchors, and the restore check reports the driver and the suite identical to the pristine copies (`git diff` on both empty afterwards). Real gates on the real tree: `--help` exit 0 and its last printed line is the new header's own, `--chunk 777` exit 2, a `nope_123` named install that is not there exits 1 and prints `models/nope_123`. `tools/lint.sh` shell, shellcheck, python and docs each exit 0, then the whole eighteen-gate `all` exits 0. The CI verdict group with the new suite registered runs 53 suites / 1,130 tests, OK. NOT CHECKED: `--verify-only` over the two real installs under `models/`, because coremltools is not installed here and the operator's TinyTitanServer is resident, so the run would either die on the interpreter or need a model process; the stub interpreter is what this suite and CI exercise. Nothing was fetched and no model was run.

### AUD-295 — `tools/lib/python.sh` tests every interpreter it searches for and none the operator names: a `TINYTITAN_PYTHON` pointing at a missing path, a Python 3.9, one without the analysis stack or a plain directory all resolve at status 0

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** tools
- **Location:** ``tools/lib/python.sh:40-43` (the override branch as shipped), :48-55 (the loop it skips), :68 (the refusal's candidate list); the call sites it feeds are `tools/install_models.sh:446` and :524, :553, :566, :599, :628, :675`
- **Category:** an operator's own choice escaping the check every found candidate has to pass: the value set by hand is the one value never tested
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** the sweep after AUD-294's close, taken over how the harnesses handle their environment. The instrument was a stub-interpreter probe: its first version exited 0 on the library's own version assert, so it proved nothing about the floor or about falling past a disqualified candidate, and that run is withdrawn; the stub was rewritten to read the required version out of the probe text and answer it honestly, and the stub was tested before any claim was kept from it.

**Evidence before.** Measured model-free on this commit by sourcing the real library in /bin/bash 3.2.57 against stubs in a temp directory, with the floor at 3.10 and the stack at numpy, ml_dtypes and safetensors. TINYTITAN_PYTHON set to a path that does not exist: status 0, that path returned. To an interpreter that reports 3.9: status 0, that path. To one that cannot import ml_dtypes: status 0. To a directory: status 0. No probe ran for any of them -- the branch at :40-43 returns before the loop, so the three screens the search applies are never applied to the one value an operator typed, which is the value most likely to contain a typo. `tools/install_models.sh:446` assigns the answer without checking it and six later call sites exec it as "$python" tools/prepare_*.py, so the failure arrives as a raw command-not-found after the download has been arranged -- the comment above :446 says resolving once exists to prevent exactly that. The search itself was re-measured and is sound: a 3.14 without the stack falls to 3.13, a candidate reporting 3.9 falls to the next, a non-executable candidate is skipped, and the bare `python` name is tried and can win (status 0). The refusal it prints when nothing qualifies says `tried (newest first): python3.14 python3.13 python3.12 python3.11 python3.10 python3`, six names, while the loop at :48-55 tries seven -- `python` is missing from the message whose whole job is to report what was tried.

**Fix.** `tools/lib/python.sh:40-67` extracts the three screens into tinytitan_python_usable(), which keeps what the candidate itself answered in $TINYTITAN_PYTHON_WHY. :72-85 runs the operator's value through it and refuses at 1, naming the value, the floor, the package check and the cause. :99 is the same call where the loop used to spell the test out, and :106 now lists all seven candidates. The library header and the resolver paragraph of docs/adding-a-model.md both claimed the override `overrides the search entirely`; both now say it skips the search and not the test.

**Evidence after.** Written first, and it failed first: RED measured 5 of 14 tests failing against the unpatched library -- the four override shapes returning status 0 and the refusal's list missing `python`. That fifth test passed for the wrong reason in its first cut: it asked whether each searched name appeared in the printed list, and `python3.14` contains `python`, so the assertion was satisfied by the wrong token; it now compares token lists in order, and against the library's own `command -v` lines rather than a restated list. GREEN: 14 tests OK, then 16 after two pins were added while designing the mutation sweep -- that the newest usable candidate wins when two of them work (every fall-through test disqualified the newer one, so newest-first itself was never asserted), and that a refusal's cause is read from its own line: the no-stack test asserted `ml_dtypes` against the whole message and was satisfied by the `need:` line, so a refusal carrying no cause at all would have passed. Suite: `benchmark/test_python_resolver_gate.py`, 16 tests, rc=0, registered in CI in the same commit. Mutation sweep over the fixed library: 18 anchored mutants, 0 bad anchors, 16 killed, 2 survivors, library identical to pristine afterwards. Both survivors are equivalent rather than untested, and one only after a test was added for its shape: dropping the `-x` screen still refuses a non-executable file, because the probe then answers Permission denied -- the new test accepts either wording, so that branch is pinned by its status and not by its message; dropping the refusal block's stderr wrapper leaves every line still on stderr, each carrying its own redirection. Gates rc=0: shell (29 scripts, system bash 3.2.57), shellcheck 0.11.0, docs, python -- the last only after `ruff format` reflowed the new file and a bare `assert` in a helper became a raised ValueError, both inside the new suite. Neighbours rc=0, 109 tests together: the new suite, `test_install_models_batch_status` and `test_install_models_menu` (both of which set TINYTITAN_PYTHON), `test_docs_facts_suites`, `test_docs_facts_gate_names`, `test_ane_sidecars_gate` and `test_release_installer_verification`; no existing fixture was edited. Real host: the resolver still answers /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14, which imports all three packages, and TINYTITAN_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3.1 now answers 1 with `it answered: no such file` instead of handing the typo on. Recorded rather than fixed: the check is by exit status alone, so a program that exits 0 for any argument passes it -- /usr/bin/true does, which is why the two installer suites use it as their override. Making the probe demand an interpreter that *answers* would refuse those two fixtures, and rewriting a test to reach green is not this row's to do quietly.

**Commit.** `5b6c2e1`

### AUD-299 — a `--web` launch given a word or a zero-padded `TINYTITAN_WARM_TOKENS` dies after the model has loaded with a bash message that names neither variable, and `TINYTITAN_WARM_TIMEOUT=0` is handed to curl as its no-timeout

- **Severity / tier:** S2 / Tier A
- **Project:** tools
- **Location:** ``tools/server_launcher.sh:1826` (the size read as shipped), :1837 (`warm_repeat=$(( warm_tokens / 11 ))`), :1838 (the clamp a 0 lands on), :1847 (the hand-off to `curl --max-time`), :1852 (the borrowed cause); the in-file precedent is the port check at :1213-1218; the guard now sits at :1238-1265 and the two reads at :1871 and :1892`
- **Category:** an operator's number read where its documented edge value means the opposite of what the caller means, and read after the expensive step rather than before it
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** named in AUD-298's sibling note and measured here. Two instruments, both model-free: the port block and the warm block taken verbatim out of the file as one script under `/bin/bash` 3.2 with a `curl` function that records every argument on its own line, and the live launcher through `launcher_fixture` with `TINYTITAN_LAUNCHER_DRY_RUN=1` so the guard is proved to be on the path a real launch takes. curl's own two semantics were measured against `/usr/bin/curl` and a 127.0.0.1 listener that accepts and never answers.

**Evidence before.** Measured against the pre-fix file (the `:NNNN` references in `test_launcher_warm_gate.py` are that revision): `abc` -> exit 1, `abc: unbound variable`, no request; `08000` -> exit 1, `value too great for base` (bash reads a leading zero as octal, so the size the operator named is not the size used); `4000.5` -> exit 1, syntax error; `-5` and `0` -> exit 0, one request, after the line has printed `~ -5 tokens` / `~ 0 tokens` and the clamp at :1838 has sent a one-repeat prompt. `TINYTITAN_WARM_TIMEOUT` was handed to curl exactly as written: `0` is what curl documents as `continue forever` -- measured, the real curl against the stalled listener did not return -- and `abc` exits non-zero naming curl, which :1852 reports as `The warm-up did not finish`, the same sentence a slow model gets. All three deaths happened after the model load and before the client opened, which is the ordering the port guard at :1213-1218 already refuses.

**Fix.** `tools/server_launcher.sh:1238-1265` checks both numbers where they are read, beside the port check and on its exit status: a `case` per value refuses a bare `0` by name (the size that warms nothing, and curl's no-timeout), a leading zero (the octal read), and anything that is not all digits, each naming the variable and what to write instead. The block is scoped `if (( WEB )) && [[ "${TINYTITAN_WARM:-1}" != "0" ]]`, so a run that never warms is not refused for a number it never reads. The warm block then reads the checked variables (:1870, :1891) instead of the environment a second time. curl's documented zero and the arithmetic's own rules are untouched: the defect was the caller reading a size as a switch, not the tool documenting one.

**Evidence after.** Written first. RED measured 10 of 20 tests failing against the launcher as shipped (`git show HEAD:` of the pre-fix file, restored afterwards and compared byte-for-byte), including the four live-path tests, which asked what a real `--web --dry-run` launch does and got a plan instead of a refusal. GREEN: 20 tests OK in 3.5 s. Neighbours 82 tests OK over `test_launcher_port`, `_ram`, `_concurrency`, `_lifetime`, `_install`, `test_dsh_port_gate`, `test_memval_run_repeats`; no existing assertion in any of them was edited. Mutation sweep: 11 anchored mutants of the guard, 0 bad anchors, 9 killed, file restored byte-identical after every one. The first pass left 3 survivors, and each was evidence about the test rather than a mutant to delete: a `0` refused by the leading-zero arm instead of its own still exits 2 with no request, so the zero test now pins the words `warms nothing` and forbids `leading zero` (added inside the new suite, no existing file touched), which kills that mutant; the other two -- the warm block and the curl call re-reading the environment instead of the checked value -- are true equivalents, because a guard that refuses rather than rewrites leaves the second read returning the same value. That finding is what disproved the new suite's own docstring claim that such a re-read `shows up as a request that reached curl`; the claim is withdrawn in the docstring and in the script's comment rather than left standing, and the sweep record here is the evidence. Gates rc=0: shell (29 scripts, system bash 3.2.57), shellcheck 0.11.0, python (ruff 0.16.7, 188 scripts parse under the 3.13 floor; one quote-style reformat of the new file, assertions unchanged), docs (83 documents, 200 ledger commit references resolved, 92/96 python suites registered in CI, table shape in all 109). The suite was `git add`ed before `.github/workflows/ci.yml` named it, per AUD-211.

**Commit.** `f17f632`

### AUD-259 — `CPUModelBackend.setContention` promises the caller sets the served CPU model's thread width from GPU activity; no caller does, so in a mixed GPU+CPU catalog the CPU model holds full width while a GPU generation runs

- **Severity / tier:** S3 / Tier B
- **Project:** server
- **Location:** `sources/TinyTitanServer/Core/CPUModelBackend.swift:175`
- **Category:** decision: a public setter whose documented caller does not exist, and wiring it changes measured performance
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** Section 6 unused-code sweep (`.build/aud258/dead.py`), the second of two survivors; AUD-258 was the other.

**Evidence before.** Measured statically, this commit. `rg -n setContention -g '*.swift'` over sources/, tests/, tools/, examples/ and plugins/ returns exactly one line: the definition at CPUModelBackend.swift:175-177. (A plain grep also lit up two Metal `.pcm`/module records under `examples/embedded/.build`; `strings` shows they hold `setContentionRelief`, an unrelated SDK symbol, so those are not callers.) The chain the setter feeds is live and does work elsewhere: `CPUQwen35.applyWidthPolicy()` (:181-184) is called before every token from `step(token:needsLogits:)` (:154), and `guard let contention else { return }` (:182) means a nil signal leaves `threads` at whatever it was. Nothing passes contention to the served backend: `CPUModelBackend.init` builds the engine as `CPUQwen35(snapshot: snapshot)` (:104) with no `threads:` argument, and that constructor's own lines (:101-102) set both `threads` and `idleThreads` to `Int8AffineGEMV.preferredThreads`. The path where the signal *is* installed is the side engine -- `SideEngine.swift:330` does `model.contention = isClientGenerating` on the model it loads in the background -- and main.swift:193 supplies `{ coordinator.generating.isBusy }` for it. The gap is the catalog: `ModelRouter.standardLoader` (:82-102) loads `.gpu` entries as sessions and `.cpu` entries as `CPUModelBackend` in the same server, so a process serving both has a GPU generation and a full-width CPU generation competing for the same performance cores. The cost is this tree's own recorded numbers, quoted in the doc comments at CPUModelBackend.swift:172-174 and CPUQwen35.swift:48-51: one thread costs a 35B generation 3%, two cost 13%, four cost 31%.

**Evidence after.** Not changed. Two candidate repairs, and they are not equivalent: (1) wire the served CPU backend to a *GPU-only* busy signal, so it narrows while a GPU generation holds the device and not while it is itself decoding; (2) delete `setContention` and reword the doc to the truth -- the width is caller-set for the side engine, which is the only place it is set, and the served CPU model runs at preferred width. Option (1) is the one the doc asks for and it cannot be written with what exists today: `coordinator.generating` (:27, `enter()`/`leave()` at :65-66) counts every generation without regard to kind, so `backend.setContention { coordinator.generating.isBusy }` would clamp the served CPU model to `busyThreads = 1` during its *own* decode -- a naive wiring that reads as correct and is the wrong semantics. A real fix therefore adds a per-kind busy signal to the coordinator or the router, which is engine-scheduling work with a numerics-adjacent cost, and it needs a model run to measure, which the operator's live server currently bars.

### AUD-293 — `watchdog_calibrate.py` answers 2 for a watchdog that fired and 1 for a corpus that is not there, while the drivers around it answer 2 for a run that measured nothing -- a wrapper reading both codes cannot tell a certified false positive from a skip

- **Severity / tier:** S3 / Tier B
- **Project:** benchmark
- **Location:** `benchmark/watchdog_calibrate.py:31-41 (its docstring table), :362-374 (the verdict), :380-382 (selftest's missing-fixture 1); benchmark/side_engine_judges.py:27-34 and benchmark/tinytitan_io_backend_ab.py:14-22 (the table the rest answer)`
- **Category:** decision: two status tables in one directory, where 2 reads as a measured disagreement in one driver and as NOT MEASURED in the rest
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-292's fix. The row named the numbering as an open question when it was filed; the repair pinned the driver's own codes rather than renumbering them, because moving them is not the auditor's call. The counts below were measured for this close.

**Evidence before.** measured on this commit, statically. 51 non-test files in `benchmark/` have a `main()` and answer a status from it -- 23 ending on `raise SystemExit(main())`, 28 on `sys.exit(main())`, none of the 51 calling `main()` and discarding it. Thirteen print their codes as a docstring table row for 2, and all thirteen mean the run produced no measurement: `side_engine_judges.py:33` `2  NOT MEASURED -- no jobs file, no done file, no rows in it, or a row that...`, `guard_source_rate.py` `2  the gate cannot be judged, with the reason named: no recorded run`, `side_engine_recall.py` and `side_engine_wired_cases.py` `2  the comparison does not exist`, `tinytitan_hit_fixup_ab.py` and `tinytitan_io_backend_ab.py:20` `2  the A/B did not run`, `tinytitan_knob_sweep.py` and `tinytitan_sampler_ab.py` `2  the headline could not be computed`, `tinytitan_v42_control_plane_ab.py` `2  the measurement does not exist`, `capital_of_paris_smartness.py` `2  a run variable was refused before the first request`, `tinytitan_ane_prefill_ab.py` and `tinytitan_mtp_phases.py` `2  it could not be compared`, `tinytitan_mtp_b3_qualification.py` `2  the gate could not be answered`. The phrase is not the whole convention: `quant_perplexity_ab.py:119` answers 2 for a missing engine binary, a refusal in the same direction, without printing a table. `watchdog_calibrate.py` is the outlier in both directions -- :370 answers 2 only for a trip it measured and :372 answers 1 for a corpus that does not exist, where 1 is what the eight call a contested measurement that did run. So the two readings of 2 are opposite: one says `a false positive was found`, the other `nothing was found, and nothing was looked for`, and `selftest()` (:382) answers the same 1 for a fixture that is not there. Nothing branches on it yet: `grep -n watchdog_calibrate` over `tools/`, `.github/`, `sources/`, `tests/` and `benchmark/` returns the CI suite name and no invocation, and the two documents that describe the driver (`docs/plan-watchdogs.md:176,232`, `docs/watchdogs.md:73,127`) quote its printouts, not its exit codes. The collision is latent, and it is the class AUD-211 and AUD-262 turned into gates: a job that runs two drivers and treats non-zero as failure with 2 held aside as a skip would report a measured false positive as a skip.

**Evidence after.** Not decided, and not changed by AUD-292's fix beyond naming it in the docstring. The auditor's recommendation, for the record: join the tree's table, because the alternative keeps one driver whose 2 means the opposite of nineteen others' 2, and the calibration's real product is its printout -- the status only has to say whether the number beside it can be trusted.

Measured negative, so nobody builds the obvious bad gate: the discard class cannot be gated by shape -- 411 sites in tests/ are `_ = try ...`, and the overwhelming majority are journal or session writes whose result is genuinely irrelevant. ### AUD-138 — Four try?-to-empty reads split off AUD-134: recall quality on a background path, and two protocol methods with no production caller

- **Severity / tier:** S3 / Tier C
- **Project:** memory
- **Location:** `sources/TinyTitanMemory/MemoryRetrieval.swift:52, :233; sources/TinyTitanMemory/ContinuityJournalStore.swift:71, :92`
- **Category:** error swallowed into an empty answer (low reach)
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** split from AUD-134 during its verification

**Evidence before.** Read and confirmed while narrowing AUD-134. MemoryRetrieval.swift:52 skips one promoted fact and :233 caches a question with an empty candidate set when the store read throws -- the cost is recall on the background retrieval path, never a wrong answer shown as right. ContinuityJournalStore.sessions():71 and search():92 both `guard let taskID = try? await store.taskID(...) else { return [] }`; they satisfy the SessionJournal protocol (SessionJournal.swift:25-28) and the only production consumer of `journalStore(for:)` is consolidation, which calls `turns()` (MemoryBackend+Consolidation.swift:88-91). Benign only while that stays true, which is why this is a row and not a dismissal.

**Fix.** Decided, per the row's own instruction, and the decision is different at each of the four sites because their consequences differ. `ContinuityJournalStore.sessions()` and `search()` propagate now (the protocol's reads are throwing, so `[]` means empty and nothing else); they still have no production caller, and that is precisely why making them honest costs nothing and leaving them swallowing would have been the row's own "benign only while that stays true" trap. `MemoryRetrieval.runQueue`'s coverage read -- the one that decides whether a question has any facts to judge -- reports once per scope through a new `reportedSweepFailures` set and drops the question, worded so the log distinguishes "nothing worth judging" from "nothing was judged": `no facts were judged for this question`. `MemoryRetrieval.applied(to:)`'s per-key `try? await store.get` is deliberately left swallowing, with the reason in the code above it: one failed fetch costs one promotion and the list that comes back is the token ranking's own, which is what the caller had before any hint existed, so the degraded answer is already honest and there is nothing to misreport.

**Evidence after.** `MemoryReadFailureTests.theHinterReportsAnUnreadableCoveragePool`: one `degraded during hint-coverage` line for the scope after a first search, and still one after a second question to the same broken store -- the once-per-scope rule, not a per-question line. Mutation check: silencing the report fails the test with 3 issues. The two protocol reads are covered by `tests/TinyTitanMemory/SessionJournalTests.swift` and the throwing-signature fallout across `ContinuityStoreTests`, `MemoryBackendTests` and `MemoryConsolidationTests`, all green in the full serial run (1612 tests, 7 targets, exit 0). The `applied(to:)` decision is recorded in the source comment at the site so the next sweep finds the reason rather than the omission.

### AUD-146 — Two expert-cache derivations read the rung list's literal order as a promise that it holds the largest value

- **Severity / tier:** S3 / Tier B
- **Project:** runtime
- **Location:** `sources/TinyTitan/Runtime/Configuration/RuntimeConfiguration.swift:245 (pre-fix), :310 (pre-fix)`
- **Category:** implicit invariant on a public constant
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-145 sibling audit

**Evidence before.** `return fitting.last ?? allowedExpertCacheSlots.first ?? 8` in `expertCacheSlotsFitting` and `let smaller = allowedExpertCacheSlots.last(where: { $0 < choice })` in the step-down loop both take the *last element in list order*, and mean the *largest value*. They agree only while `allowedExpertCacheSlots` is written ascending -- nothing pinned that, and the list is `public`, with rungs added by hand over time (the comment records 112 added, then 160/192/256 on 2026-09-05). An insertion in the wrong place would silently hand the cache a smaller-but-not-largest fitting count, or step down to a rung that is not the nearest below: the same function whose own comment describes a 34%-overshoot paging cliff (0.42 against 2.01 tok/s) that the step-down exists to prevent.

**Fix.** The two derivations state the value they mean: `fitting.max() ?? Self.minimumExpertCacheSlots`, and a `let rungs = allowedExpertCacheSlots.sorted()` taken before the step-down loop, so `last(where:)` reads a sorted list rather than a literal's spelling. One order assumption remains on purpose -- the nearest-rung walk settles a tie on the earlier element, which is the smaller rung only while the list climbs -- and the code says so and the new test pins it. Found while fixing AUD-145; committed with it rather than left as a note, because the audit step that found it is the same one that had the differential test in hand.

**Evidence after.** The AUD-145 differential is also this row's: the sorted/`max()` forms matched the order-dependent forms at all 672 grid points x 2 functions, which is exactly the claim that the rewrite is value-preserving while the list climbs. The order itself is now enforced: swapping the literal's first two rungs (`16, 8, 24, ...`) made `expertCacheSlotFloorIsTheSmallestRung` record `Expectation failed: RuntimeConfiguration.allowedExpertCacheSlots == RuntimeConfiguration.allowedExpertCacheSlots.sorted()` -- 2 issues in that run (the floor and the order), suite failed, then restored and green. The behavioural suites stayed green under the reorder, which is the point of the fix: with `max()` and a sorted copy, a reordered literal cannot mis-size a cache. Full serial suite 1,614 tests in 241 suites, exit 0; all eleven gates rc 0.

### AUD-147 — readJsonBody never inspects content-type, so the second mitigation AUD-132 assumed does not exist

- **Severity / tier:** S3 / Tier A
- **Project:** fleet
- **Location:** `plugins/dsh-lan-manager/src/router.js:61-87`
- **Category:** single-layer CSRF defence recorded as two-layer
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-132 verification (the row's own 'mitigating facts', checked)

**Evidence before.** AUD-132's note claimed the JSON routes require `content-type: application/json`, which a cross-origin simple form POST cannot set. Read the function: readJsonBody (router.js:61) collects bytes under the cap and calls JSON.parse on whatever arrives, with no header check on any path, so `enctype="text/plain"` -- one of the three content types a browser form may send without a preflight -- carries a valid JSON object straight through. No browser hole is open today, because such a POST always carries Origin and Guard 3 refuses a foreign one; the defect is that the defence is single-layer while the tree believes it is two, and any future change that loosens Guard 3 (`config.enforceOrigin !== false` is a documented off switch) silently removes the only check. Both real senders already set the header -- FleetClient.swift:89 sets `application/json` for every body it writes -- so requiring it costs no client. Decide, do not assume: whether to refuse a bodied request whose content-type is not JSON, and whether the plugin's own served UI posts through a path that sets it (plugins/dsh-lan-manager has no web/ assets; the page is served by the harness bundle, so the answer must be read there before the rule is written).

**Fix.** `readJsonBody` refuses with 415 `unsupported-media-type` unless `content-type` starts with `application/json` (case-folded). The check sits after the empty-body early return, so a bodiless POST still passes — the shape `FleetClient.swift:89` writes, which sets the header for every body and none for an empty request — and the README's `curl` examples already set it, so no sender in the tree breaks. README layer 4 records the point of the layer: it does not depend on Guard 3, so `enforceOrigin: false` is no longer an off switch for the only body check. Suite re-run on current main at ef30d5f: `node --test` in plugins/dsh-lan-manager prints `tests 122 / suites 0 / pass 122 / fail 0 / cancelled 0 / skipped 0` (260 ms), and `tools/lint.sh javascript` prints `ok: dsh-lan-manager` and `ok: dsh-tinytitan` (node v26.10.0, eslint 10.11.0, prettier 3.9.9). Nothing was pushed.

**Evidence after.** Commit ef30d5f. `test/router.test.js` pins three shapes: a `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` post -> 415, a `text/plain` body holding a valid JSON object -> 415 (the exact payload AUD-132 assumed was blocked), and `application/json; charset=utf-8` -> accepted, which is why the rule is a prefix test and not equality. The pre-existing `malformed JSON is a 400 with a stable code` returned 415 once the guard landed, because its raw iterator bypassed the header; it was rewritten to send `raw: "{not json"` through the helper so it still pins the parse path — that rewrite is the evidence the new guard did not silently absorb the old assertion. Mutation check M1 (guard deleted) fails 2 tests.

**Commit.** `ef30d5f`

### AUD-148 — isAllowedOrigin calls an origin same-origin whenever its host equals the request's Host, which is the DNS-rebinding shape

- **Severity / tier:** S3 / Tier A
- **Project:** fleet
- **Location:** `plugins/dsh-lan-manager/src/router.js:244`
- **Category:** trust boundary decided by an attacker-supplied header pair
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-132 sibling audit

**Evidence before.** `if (host && parsed.host === host) return true;` compares the Origin against the request's own Host header, so equality is granted by the attacker's naming, not by anything the server knows. A page served from an attacker domain that resolves to 127.0.0.1 (a TTL-0 record, the classic rebinding) and reaches the harness on its own port sends Origin: http://attacker.example:<port> with Host: attacker.example:<port> -- equal, so allowed, and the mutating routes are open to it. Two facts narrow it and belong in the row: it needs the attacker's page served on the *same port* the harness listens on, and a shared token (Guard 2) defeats it outright -- but the token is opt-in, `config.token` empty means Guard 2 is skipped entirely (router.js:172). The shape of the fix is a Host allowlist the server knows (127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1, and the host's own configured base path authority) instead of an origin-equals-host equality, and the decision belongs with AUD-147, since both change the same guard. Not verified live: no rebinding harness was run here; the claim is read from the code and is stated as such.

**Fix.** Same-origin is now decided by something the server knows. `isKnownHost(authority, config)` accepts `localhost`, an address literal inside the configured networks (via `checkAddress`, which is why bracketed `[fe80::1%en0]:3080` and zone ids work), and a name in `trustedHosts` or `trustedOrigins`; `isAllowedOrigin`'s host branch requires `parsed.host === host && isKnownHost(host, config)` instead of the bare equality, so attacker-supplied naming no longer grants the pair. New config key `trustedHosts` with `DSH_LAN_TRUSTED_HOSTS` is the operator's escape hatch for a real hostname. Decision recorded: an explicit allowlist rather than deriving the host's own authorities from the socket, because the plugin is mounted in a server it does not own and cannot read its bind address. `HTTPServerHandler+Routes.swift:43-45` was read for the same shape; it sits behind the loopback-only bind and was left alone. Suite re-run on current main at ef30d5f: `node --test` in plugins/dsh-lan-manager prints `tests 122 / suites 0 / pass 122 / fail 0 / cancelled 0 / skipped 0` (260 ms), and `tools/lint.sh javascript` prints `ok: dsh-lan-manager` and `ok: dsh-tinytitan` (node v26.10.0, eslint 10.11.0, prettier 3.9.9). Nothing was pushed.

**Evidence after.** Commit ef30d5f. `test/router.test.js` pins the rebinding shape end to end: Origin `http://attacker.invalid:3080` presented with the matching Host -> 403, where it was 200 before the fix; `trustedHosts: ["lan-desk.local"]` makes that pair 200 while `elsewhere.example` with its own matching Host stays 403, so the allowlist is an addition rather than a removal of the equality rule. `isKnownHost` has its own table test: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1:3080`, `::1`, `10.0.0.5:3080` and `[fe80::1%en0]:3080` trusted; `attacker.invalid:3080`, `8.8.8.8` and the empty string refused. Mutation check M2 (bare `parsed.host === host` restored) fails 3 tests.

**Commit.** `ef30d5f`

### AUD-151 — The 500-line production-file standard has no gate, and three files exceed it while the layout doc still states that none do

- **Severity / tier:** S3 / Tier C
- **Project:** lint-gates
- **Location:** `docs/repository-layout.md:135-140 (the claim), sources/TinyTitanLib/Engine.swift:529, sources/TinyTitanLib/OpenAIRequestValidator.swift:521, sources/TinyTitan/Runtime/Prefill/ANEPrefillAttention.swift:519 (the tree)`
- **Category:** missing gate, contract drift / stale documentation on a load-bearing rule
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-142 fix, sibling sweep (the file-length measurement taken to keep this row's own additions inside the standard)

**Evidence before.** `AGENTS.md` states the rule (a file under `sources/` stays at 500 physical lines or fewer, comments and blanks included, `tests/` exempt) and `docs/repository-layout.md:137` records it as fact, in the present tense: 'No file under `sources/` is above it as of 2026-09-28 — git ls-files 'sources/**/*.swift' | xargs wc -l lists 353 files and the largest is under the limit'. Measured 2026-10-06 with that same command, three are over it: `TinyTitanLib/Engine.swift` 529, `TinyTitanServer/Core/OpenAIRequestValidator.swift` 521, `TinyTitan/Runtime/Prefill/ANEPrefillAttention.swift` 519. Nothing in `tools/lint.sh` checks file length — `func-length` measures functions, and swiftlint's own file-length rule is not in the committed config — so the standard is carried entirely by the habit of whoever last touched each file. The evidence that habit is not enough is this sweep's own row: AUD-142 added 4 lines to `Engine.swift` (525 -> 529) and 7 to `ANEPrefillAttention.swift` (512 -> 519), and neither the compiler nor any of the twelve gates then running objected. Both files were already over before it.

**Fix.** Both halves of the row are done: the three files are split and the number is now a gate.

* `Engine.swift` 529 -> 286; the configuration vocabulary (`EngineConfiguration`, `InstallIntegrity`, `CachePrecision`, `RoPEScaling`, `ThinkingMode`, `ReasoningEffort`, `ReadAheadAdvice`, `SamplingDefaults`) moved to `EngineConfiguration.swift` (257). Nothing was widened: every declaration there was already `public` or module-internal.
* `ANEPrefillAttention.swift` 519 -> 431; the sidecar contract (where its directory lives for a configured chunk width, what `ane_prefill.json` records, and the bounded read of that document) moved to `ANEPrefillAttention+Sidecar.swift` (99), joining the `+Models.swift` sibling already in that directory. Nothing was widened, because nothing there was `private`.
* `OpenAIRequestValidator.swift` 521 -> 302; the nested-input validators (`validateTool`, `validateSchemaKeys`, `requireSchemaDepth`, `validateMessages`), the `structuredOutputSchema` they share and the `invalid` constructor moved to `OpenAIRequestValidator+Structure.swift` (234). Five members went `private` -> `internal`, which is the cost of the split: `private` is file-scoped in Swift. No `public` surface moved.

`tools/lint.sh` gains `file-length` as its fourteenth check: every `*.swift` under `sources/` counted in physical lines, as the written rule counts them, against `MAX_FILE_LINES` (500). It prints a `SCANNED:`/`LARGEST:` receipt, fails on a zero-scanned tree and on a counter that did not run, and has **no exemption row and no baseline file** -- deliberately, because `func-length` ratchets only because 1,449-line functions cannot all be decomposed in one pass, while a 501-line file can be split in one.

Two corrections, forward rather than silent. (1) This row's `file_line` named `sources/TinyTitanServer/Core/OpenAIRequestValidator.swift`, which has not existed since 715df2c and 0cdba76 moved it to `sources/TinyTitanLib/`; the `evidence-before` above keeps the original wording verbatim, and the file that was split is the `TinyTitanLib` one -- it was, and still is, the 521-line file. (2) The gate's scope is narrower than the prose: it sweeps `*.swift`, so `.metal` shader sources (610-1,377 lines) and `tests/` sit outside it, and the gate's own comment says so and why rather than hiding the difference. `AGENTS.md` still enumerates thirteen checks and still says "a file under `sources/`"; both are the owner's edits, and this row does not make them.

`docs/repository-layout.md` and `docs/audit-2026-10-06/tool-coverage.md` carry the split table and the five-arm probe.

**Evidence after.** Done at b1da18a.

* The splits are proved to be code motion, not rewritten code: a line-multiset (`Counter`) comparison of `HEAD:<pre-split file>` against the union of the post-split files prints only the asymmetric difference. It printed **zero removed lines** for `Engine.swift` and `ANEPrefillAttention.swift`, and exactly the five `private static func` signature lines for `OpenAIRequestValidator.swift` -- i.e. the widenings and nothing else.
* The gate was probed in a copied tree (`/tmp/fl-gate`), because `tools/lint.sh` derives and re-exports its own `ROOT`, so a caller-supplied `ROOT` never reaches a check; the first four arms were vacuous before that was found. Five arms, six results, all as expected: the pre-split 529-line file -> exit 1 `OVER 529 sources/Engine.swift`; post-split -> exit 0; a file at exactly 500 -> exit 0 and at 501 -> exit 1 (boundary is `> limit`, as the rule reads); a `sources/` with no Swift -> exit 1 'found no Swift sources'; `PATH=/nonexistent` -> exit 1 'the length counter exited 127; it measured nothing'.
* `swift build -c release` -> `Build complete! (98.27 sec)`, exit 0.
* `swift test --no-parallel` -> exit 0: 1,645 tests in 246 suites across seven targets, 0 failures.
* All fourteen gates: `tools/lint.sh` exit 0 (`/tmp/tt-audit/lint-final-aud151.log`).
* `tools/golden-baseline.sh --check qwen38-4` -> `== qwen38-4 == ok - output identical to baseline`, exit 0, after the model preconditions were checked (macOS 27.0.1, Swift 6.4, 344 GB free, `memory_pressure -Q` 81% free, no process matching the model-process list). The default target `ornith-8` is **not checked**: that install is not in `models/`, and no model is fetched to satisfy a gate.

### AUD-152 — `swift build -c release --build-tests` failed to resolve every test module's dependency on a tree that builds clean, and did not re-produce

- **Severity / tier:** S3 / Tier C
- **Project:** tooling
- **Location:** `observed while running `swift build -c release --build-tests` on the tree at 65bf241; log /tmp/audit143-build.log (not committed — scratch), against Package.swift's test targets`
- **Category:** build invocation that cannot pass on this tree, mis-read as a flake: a release `--build-tests` compiles product libraries without -enable-testing, so a @testable import has nothing to bind
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-143 diagnosis, 2026-10-06, while trying to get a release-config test bundle to run

**Evidence before.** One occurrence, recorded rather than chased, and the reason it was not chased is the point. The command `swift build -c release --build-tests` reported, for each of seven test modules' product dependencies — ContinuityCore, TinyTitanFleetCore, TinyTitanMemory, TinyTitanRepackCore, TinyTitan, TinyTitanLib, TinyTitanServerCore — `unable to resolve Swift module dependency to a compatible module '<name>'`, then `Build failed`. The same tree built clean in debug at that commit, and the very next invocation, `swift test -c release`, printed `Build complete! (129.06 sec)` and ran the suite. So the failure was real for that invocation and gone for the next one, with no change to the tree between them.
    It was not re-produced deliberately. The only way to force the condition again is to discard the release build directory so the graph has to be resolved from scratch, and the standing constraints for this repository forbid purging caches just to run a check; a flake that needs a destructive step to reproduce is not worth that trade on a single occurrence. Consequence to weigh: an unresolved-module error of this shape reads as a manifest or dependency defect, so a future session that meets it will be tempted into exactly that purge, or into editing Package.swift on a false premise. Recording it here is what stops that.
    CORRECTED FORWARD on 2026-10-06: it is not a flake and it does re-produce, and the earlier reading that it needed a destructive cache purge to bring back was wrong. `swift build -c release --build-tests` failed 2 of 2 on a tree that debug-builds clean, naming `TinyTitanFleetCore` once and seven modules the other time — the set is whatever the build reaches before it stops. `swift test -c release` on the same tree printed `Build complete! (148.88 sec)` and ran the suite, which is why the first occurrence read as self-healing: the next command was a different command. The mechanism was then measured rather than guessed — adding `-Xswiftc -enable-testing` to the failing invocation makes it succeed, `Build complete! (147.46 sec)`. A release `--build-tests` compiles the local libraries that back the products without `-enable-testing`, and the eight modules named in the errors are exactly the ones the tests `@testable import` (grep: TinyTitan 138 files, TinyTitanLib 41, TinyTitanServerCore 34, TinyTitanRepackCore 27, TinyTitanMemory 16, ContinuityCore 8, TinyTitanFleetCore 2, TinyTitanCLICore 2).

**Fix.** Diagnosed, and the consequence is a command choice rather than a code change: release-configuration test runs use `swift test -c release`, never `swift build -c release --build-tests`; if a workflow genuinely needs the latter, `-Xswiftc -enable-testing` is the flag that makes it work. `tools/tsan-storm.sh:62` runs `swift build --build-tests --sanitize=thread` — debug, where testing is enabled — so no script in this repository depends on the failing invocation, and `Package.swift` needed nothing. Recorded where the next session meets it before the failure: the traps section of docs/handover-tinytitan.md, which says explicitly not to purge `.build` or edit the manifest when this error appears. That instruction is the point of the row: the error reads as a manifest or dependency defect, and the only way to force it again as first filed was a cache purge — a destructive step taken on a false premise.

**Evidence after.** The traps section of docs/handover-tinytitan.md is committed with this ledger write — the audit commit that follows 07e867b, which carries the code and the measurements rather than the prose. Measurements in evidence-before: 2 of 2 fail plain, 1 of 1 succeed with `-Xswiftc -enable-testing`, 1 of 1 succeed as `swift test -c release`, same tree, no cache touched. Not re-produced a third time on purpose — the rule is now explained by the flag that changes the outcome, and the standing constraint against purging build directories still applies.

**Commit.** `07e867b`

### AUD-154 — Every group-facing response echoes the shared group key in cleartext, so the string that authorises the API lands in logs, dumps and screenshots

- **Severity / tier:** S3 / Tier A
- **Project:** fleet
- **Location:** `plugins/dsh-lan-manager/src/router.js (/health, /peers, /inventory bodies) and src/peers.js:302-312`
- **Category:** secret disclosure on an authenticated surface, found by the AUD-123/147/148 sibling audit
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-147/AUD-148 sibling sweep, 2026-10-06

**Evidence before.** Read from the code, not run: `/health` returns `group: config.groupKey ?? null`, `/peers` and `/inventory` return the same field, and `peers.js:302-312` compares a peer's `body.group` against `config.groupKey` as a *literal*. So the exact value that passes Guard 2 — the only thing distinguishing two machines inside Guard 1's ranges, per config.js's own doc comment — is emitted by the three endpoints an operator is most likely to `curl` and paste into an issue, and by every gossip round that reads a peer's list. Two facts bound it and belong in the row. (1) It is not an unauthenticated leak: all three routes sit behind Guard 2, so a caller who can read the key out of a body already has it. The exposure is the second-order one — the secret in log files, captured JSON, terminal scrollback and screenshots. (2) Any replacement has to keep a mixed-version fleet talking: `peers.js` compares the literal today, so a hash-only change makes every old peer look like it is in another group and silently empties the table. That is why the fix is a digest plus a temporary dual-accept rather than a swap, and why it was not folded into ef30d5f, which changed the guards, not the payloads.

**Fix.** The key is off the wire. `groupDigest(key)` (config.js) is a domain-separated SHA-256 over `dsh-lan-group:<key>` truncated to 16 hex, computed once at resolve time, and `/health`, `/peers` and `/inventory` name the group with it instead of the literal. `groupLabel` accompanies it only while the key is the shipped default, which is published anyway and which an unconfigured fleet reads on its own screen to recognise itself. `PeerTable.probe` matches the digest *and*, as a rollout allowance, the old literal and the label — the constraint this row named: the comparison was literal, so a hash-only swap empties every peer table on upgrade. The refusal log no longer interpolates `body.group`, because a foreign peer's group string is that peer's credential rather than a diagnostic. README states the limit of the change as plainly as the change: a digest is not a second secret, since a low-entropy key is offline-testable against it, so what this removes is the copy, which is the case that actually happens.

**Evidence after.** Commit 78d3847. `test/router.test.js` `a group-facing body names the group by digest, never by the key` sets `groupKey` to a value nothing publishes, reads all three endpoints, and asserts both `body.group === groupDigest(secret)` and `JSON.stringify(res.body).includes(secret) === false` — the leak check is on the serialized body, so a future field cannot re-add the key unnoticed; the same test pins that the shipped default still gets its `groupLabel`. `groupDigest is stable, key-specific, and absent with no key` pins determinism, that two keys differ, the 16-hex shape, and `null` for null/undefined/empty. `test/peers.test.js` `the group matches by digest, by the old literal, and by the default label` runs four spellings through the real probe (digest, legacy literal, digest plus label, no group field at all) and expects each to join the table; `a foreign group string is refused without being copied into our log` asserts the refusal *and* that the log line does not contain the foreign value. Mutation checks, each restored afterwards: bodies back to `config.groupKey` -> 2 tests fail (the leak test and the `/peers` light list); legacy literal acceptance removed -> 1 fail; the reported value interpolated into the log -> 1 fail. Suite 128 tests, 128 pass, 0 fail; `tools/lint.sh javascript` prints ok for both plugin packages. The Swift client needing no change was run rather than reasoned: `FleetCommands.swift:166` only carries the string to the dashboard header, `FleetTests.swift:122` asserts against the test's own hand-written fixture, and `swift test --no-parallel --filter Fleet` returned `Test run with 48 tests in 12 suites passed after 0.336 seconds` with exit 0 (the filter matched more than the three suites named, so the run was wider than asked for, not narrower).

**Commit.** `78d3847`

### AUD-155 — The default IPv4 allowlist still admits 169.254.0.0/16, so on a network with no DHCP every host on the segment is inside the fence

- **Severity / tier:** S3 / Tier A
- **Project:** fleet
- **Location:** `plugins/dsh-lan-manager/src/net.js:39 (DEFAULT_IPV4_NETWORKS)`
- **Category:** permissive default left open deliberately by AUD-123's fix
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-123 fix, 2026-10-06 (the half that commit did not take)

**Evidence before.** `DEFAULT_IPV4_NETWORKS` carries `["169.254.0.0", 16]` next to loopback, RFC 1918 and CGNAT. On an ad-hoc segment — no DHCP server, a direct Thunderbolt pair, a conference network — every host self-assigns out of that range, so membership in Guard 1's allowlist is granted by the medium rather than by the operator, which is the property the fence exists to decide. What bounds the severity today, read from the tree rather than assumed: the harness webserver binds loopback only (index.js:232-240, the same fact that caps AUD-123), so there is no working cross-machine path yet; and since ef30d5f a *mutating* request from such a host that presents the shipped key is refused, so on an unconfigured install the exposure is reads (`/workspaces`, `/sessions`, `/sessions/:id/messages` — session content) rather than writes. With an operator-chosen key the link-local host can mutate as soon as it is given the key, which is Guard 2 working as designed and not this row's defect. Why it was not simply deleted in ef30d5f: link-local is a legitimate peer address for a directly coupled pair of Macs, and discovery returns whatever addresses the interfaces hold, so removing it from the defaults is a behaviour change for a use case the plugin documents — it needs the same decide-and-record treatment AUD-148 got, not a one-line edit.

**Fix.** Kept the ranges and narrowed what the shipped key buys from them — the decision the row owed, taken on measured ground rather than as the one-line deletion it first looked like. `isLinkLocal` (net.js) answers `169.254.0.0/16` or `fe80::/10`; Guard 2c refuses every route but the group ones (`/`, `/health`, `/peers`) to a link-local source presenting the key equal to `DEFAULT_GROUP_KEY`, `403 default-group-key-link-local-source`, sharing Guard 2b's hint through one `defaultKeyRefusal` so the two cannot drift apart. Candidate (a) — drop `169.254.0.0/16` from the defaults — was rejected on the code: `PeerTable.probe` reads `/inventory` (peers.js:297), so refusing a range is not narrowing a read, it is no mesh at all, and it would break the directly-coupled pair the plugin documents in order to close an accident. Candidate (b) as filed — gate reads fleet-wide — was rejected for the same reason read back: `/inventory` is the manager's only view, so it would have broken the tailnet fleet that is this plugin's stated shape. What is left bites only the combination that has no operator behind it: a self-assigned address *and* a key the operator never changed. `fe80::/10` stays admitted (every IPv6 host holds one, and Bonjour answers with it) but is now inside the same rule, so the asymmetry the row worried about does not exist.

**Evidence after.** Commit 78d3847. `test/net.test.js` `isLinkLocal names the ranges a host gives itself` pins both boundaries (`169.254.255.255` yes, `febf::9` yes, `fec0::1` no — so the /10 is a mask and not a string prefix), the IPv4-mapped spelling `::ffff:169.254.5.6` reaching the same verdict as the dotted one, and the cross-check that every link-local address is *also* inside the default fence and *not* loopback — which is what stops the three predicates (reachable, this machine, named itself) from quietly collapsing into one another. `test/router.test.js` `the shipped default key buys a link-local source membership, not content` drives the real handler from `169.254.9.9` and `fe80::1%en0` across 2 membership routes (200) and 6 content routes (403 with the named code), `/sessions/:id/messages`, `/workspaces/:id/sessions` and `/peers/:id` among them; then asserts the two things that make this a rule instead of a break — `/inventory` from `100.64.9.9` with the shipped key still answers 200, and `/inventory` from `169.254.9.9` answers 200 once an operator key is set. Guard order is pinned by the earlier AUD-123 test, which still expects `default-group-key-outside-loopback` for a *mutation* from the same link-local source, because 2b runs first. Mutation check: Guard 2c deleted -> 1 test fails; restored. Suite 128/128 and the javascript gate ok. Consequence recorded where a future reader will meet it: a peer that Guard 2c will not give content to is also a peer the mesh cannot list, because the probe reads `/inventory` — stated in peers.js's rule 1 and in the README, with setting a key as the fix rather than a mystery.

**Commit.** `78d3847`

### AUD-158 — Nothing enforces the library facade: `public` in `TinyTitanLib` is a promise carried only by the reviewer's memory, and so are 'imports no NIO' and 'keeps stdout clean'

- **Severity / tier:** S3 / Tier C
- **Project:** lint-gates
- **Location:** `AGENTS.md 'Two products, one repository' rules 1 and 3, sources/TinyTitanLib/*.swift (22 public types, 88 public declarations, 291 package), tools/lint.sh (no facade check)`
- **Category:** unenforced documented standard (missing gate)
- **Status:** DONE
- **Host:** Mac (primary)
- **Discovered by:** AUD-151 fix, sibling sweep (asking which other written standards are carried by habit alone)

**Evidence before.** AGENTS.md states three properties of `sources/TinyTitanLib/` as rules: every public declaration there is deliberate and 'nothing becomes `public` by accident' (rule 3, with `package` named as the default for everything internal); the library 'imports no NIO' (rule 1); and nothing in it may `print`, because stdout belongs to the embedding program. `tools/lint.sh` has fourteen checks and none of them looks at access level, imports or stdout in that target; swiftlint's config has no such rule either; and `Package.swift` grants `TinyTitanLib` whatever it declares. Measured 2026-10-06, all three properties hold: 22 public types (Engine, Session, EngineConfiguration and its seven vocabulary enums/structs, ChatMessage/Role/Prompt/GenerationOptions/GenerationEvent/GenerationSummary/GenerationStopReason/DecodeStopReason/ToolCall/ToolDefinition, ModelDescriptor, TinyTitanError), 88 public declarations against 291 `package`, no `import NIO*` in the target, and zero `print(` / `FileHandle.standardOutput` occurrences. The finding is not a violation today, it is that the standard has no teeth: adding one `public func` to `ServerModelSession.swift` or one stray `print("loaded")` to the loading path is a permanent API promise or a corrupted consumer stdout, and the compiler, the fourteen gates and the tests all stay silent. That is the same failure mode AUD-151 just closed for file length - a number stated in prose, carried by habit, and quietly out of date within a week - and this one is on the surface an external package depends on, which is what `examples/embedded` exists to prove still builds.

**Fix.** One gate, `tools/lint.sh library-facade`, and it is in the `all` chain, so CI runs it without a workflow edit. The row's `evidence-after` asked for the three properties as data; what landed holds them with two mechanisms because they are two kinds of promise. (a) The public surface is a ratchet over `tools/library-facade-baseline.txt`, one row per *declaration* (88 rows, `path:kind:name`), not one per type: the row left that choice to `docs/plan-embedded-library.md` and the owner, and the wider reading costs nothing here while being strictly stronger -- it is what lets the gate see one of `Session.respond`'s two overloads vanish behind its twin's exemption, which a per-type list cannot. Comparison is a multiset (`sort` without `-u`) for exactly that reason. NEW and STALE both fail, so an exemption cannot be reused, and a *missing* allowlist fails rather than blessing the tree -- the deliberate path is `FACADE_UPDATE=1 tools/lint.sh library-facade`, which rewrites the file so the diff is what a reviewer reads. (b) Rule 1 has no baseline and no opt-out because its correct count is zero: `tools/library-facade-rules.py` flags `import …NIO` and any stdout write (`print(`/`printf(`/`puts(`/`FileHandle.standardOutput`/`stdout`), skipping comment lines -- it must, because `ServerLog.swift`'s doc comment states this rule back at itself and a gate that fails on prose is a gate people learn to distrust.

Two scanner properties the first probe found and the code now handles, neither of which the row asked for: `open` is a wider promise than `public` (it also grants overridability outside the module) so it counts as surface, and leading attributes are stripped before the modifier is tested -- a matcher that only looks at what a line starts with would have missed `@discardableResult public func` entirely, which is the same blind spot as the `public`/`package` split it was written to police. Neither form exists in the library today, so the measured surface is unchanged at 88 and the widened matcher found nothing new; it is proved by the mutation, not by a diff.

The row's own numbers are stale and corrected forward: it says `tools/lint.sh` has fourteen checks, and by the time this was worked the script ran fifteen (file-length and test-hollow landed after the row was filed, `unbounded-read` before). `22 public types / 88 declarations / 291 package / zero NIO / zero print` re-measured as exact.

The sibling defect this surfaced is in the documentation of the gate set, and this commit is a live instance of it: `library-facade` made the counts in `RELEASE.md` and `ci.yml`'s step name wrong the moment it landed, which is AUD-160's whole claim. **Evidence after.** Clean tree: `tools/lint.sh library-facade` exits 0 with `ok (88 public declarations, all allowlisted)` and `ok (no NIO import, no stdout write, in 33 files)`.

Sixteen mutation arms, run against the live tree and reverted (full table in `docs/audit-2026-10-06/tool-coverage.md`): 16/16 behaved as required. - **Severity / tier:** S3 / Tier C
- **Project:** docs-gates
